bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第241卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 241.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 241.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十】起屠維作噩，盡昭陽赤奮若，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 60] From Tuyu Zuo'e through Zhaoyang Chifenruo—five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 60] From the jiyou year through the guichou year—five years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，亓志紹與成德合兵掠貝州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Qi Zhishao joined forces with Chengde and raided Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Qi Zhishao allied with Chengde and plundered Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 義成行營兵三千人先屯齊州，使之禹城，中道潰叛，橫海節度使李祐討誅之。

translations.literal: Three thousand troops of the Yicheng expeditionary camp were first stationed at Qizhou and ordered to Yucheng; midway they mutinied and scattered. Li You, military governor of Henghai, pursued and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand men of the Yicheng expeditionary force had been posted at Qizhou and sent on toward Yucheng, but they mutinied en route. Li You, governor of Henghai, hunted them down and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 李聽、史唐合兵擊亓志紹，破之。

translations.literal: Li Ting and Shi Tang combined their forces to attack Qi Zhishao and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting and Shi Tang joined forces, attacked Qi Zhishao, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 志紹將其眾五千奔鎮州。

translations.literal: Zhishao led his five thousand followers in flight to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishao fled to Zhenzhou with five thousand of his men.

sentences.zh: 李載義奏攻滄州長蘆，拔之。

translations.literal: Li Zaiyi memorialized that he had attacked Changlu in Cangzhou and taken it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi reported that he had attacked Changlu in Cangzhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，昭義奏亓志紹餘眾萬五千人詣本道降，置之洛州。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Zhaoyi reported that fifteen thousand survivors of Qi Zhishao's forces had come to that circuit to surrender and were settled in Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Zhaoyi reported that fifteen thousand of Qi Zhishao's remaining troops had surrendered to the circuit and were resettled in Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，橫海節度使李祐帥諸道行營兵擊李同捷，破之，進攻德州。

translations.literal: In the second month, Li You, military governor of Henghai, led the allied expeditionary forces of the various circuits against Li Tongjie, defeated him, and pressed the attack on Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Li You of Henghai led the multi-circuit expeditionary army against Li Tongjie, defeated him, and advanced on Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 武寧捉生兵馬使石雄，勇敢，愛士卒。

translations.literal: Shi Xiong, the Wuning officer in charge of prisoner-taking cavalry, was brave and cared for his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong, Wuning's officer for captive-raiding cavalry, was courageous and beloved by his troops.

sentences.zh: 王智興殘虐，軍中欲逐智興而立雄。

translations.literal: Wang Zhixing was cruel and tyrannical; the army wished to drive out Zhixing and install Xiong in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing ruled with cruelty, and the troops wanted to oust him and make Shi Xiong commander instead.

sentences.zh: 智興知之，因雄立功，奏請除刺史。

translations.literal: Zhixing learned of this; citing Xiong's meritorious service, he memorialized requesting that Xiong be appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing learned of the plot and, citing Xiong's battlefield merit, had him recommended for a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以雄為壁州剌史。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Xiong was appointed prefect of Bizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Shi Xiong was made prefect of Bizhou.

sentences.zh: 史憲誠聞滄景將平而懼，其子唐勸之入朝。

translations.literal: Shi Xiancheng, hearing that Cang and Jing were about to be pacified, grew fearful; his son Tang urged him to go to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xiancheng heard that the Cang-Jing rebellion was nearing defeat, he grew alarmed, and his son Tang urged him to present himself at court.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，憲誠使唐奉表請入朝，且請以所管聽命。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Xiancheng sent Tang to submit a memorial requesting to come to court and asking that his jurisdiction be placed under imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Xiancheng sent Tang to court with a memorial asking permission to attend in person and offering to place his command under central authority.

sentences.zh: 石雄既去武寧，王智興悉殺軍中與雄善者百餘人。

translations.literal: After Shi Xiong had left Wuning, Wang Zhixing killed more than a hundred men in the army who were on good terms with Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Xiong had left Wuning, Wang Zhixing executed more than a hundred soldiers who had been close to him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊午，智興奏雄搖動軍情，請誅之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuwu, Zhixing memorialized that Xiong had stirred up military sentiment and requested his execution.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuwu, Zhixing accused Shi Xiong of subverting troop loyalty and asked that he be put to death.

sentences.zh: 上知雄無罪，免死，長流白州。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Xiong was innocent, spared his life, and banished him far to Baizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Xiong was innocent, the emperor spared his life and exiled him to distant Baizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，李載義奏攻滄州，破其羅城。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Li Zaiyi memorialized that he had attacked Cangzhou and breached its outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Li Zaiyi reported that he had assaulted Cangzhou and broken through its outer ramparts.

sentences.zh: 李祐拔德州，城中將卒三千餘人奔鎮州。

translations.literal: Li You captured Dezhou; more than three thousand officers and soldiers in the city fled to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li You took Dezhou, and more than three thousand of its garrison fled to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 李同捷與祐書請降，祐並奏其書，諫議大夫柏耆受詔宣慰行營，好張大聲勢以威制諸將，諸將已惡之矣。

translations.literal: Li Tongjie sent Li You a letter requesting surrender; You forwarded the letter in a memorial. Bai Qi, remonstrance counsellor, received an edict to go and comfort the expeditionary camp; he liked to inflate his display of power to overawe the generals, and the generals already hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tongjie wrote Li You offering surrender, and You forwarded the letter to court. Bai Qi, a remonstrance counsellor, was ordered to the expeditionary camp as imperial envoy; he loved to parade his authority to intimidate the commanders, who already detested him.

sentences.zh: 及李同捷請降於祐，祐遣大將萬洪代守滄州。

translations.literal: When Li Tongjie requested surrender from You, You sent his great general Wan Hong to take over the defense of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongjie sued for peace through You, You sent his senior general Wan Hong to hold Cangzhou in his stead.

sentences.zh: 耆疑同捷之詐，自將數百騎馳入滄州，以事誅洪，取同捷及其家屬詣京師。

translations.literal: Qi suspected Tongjie's surrender was a ruse; he personally led several hundred horsemen in a dash into Cangzhou, found occasion to execute Hong, seized Tongjie and his family, and escorted them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting a trick, Qi rode into Cangzhou at the head of several hundred cavalry, had Hong killed on a pretext, seized Tongjie and his household, and hurried them toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，至將陵，或言王庭湊欲以奇兵篡同捷，乃斬同捷，傳首，滄景悉平。

translations.literal: On yihai, they reached Jiangling; some said Wang Tingcou intended to seize Tongjie with a surprise force, so Tongjie was beheaded and his head sent on; Cang and Jing were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, at Jiangling, word came that Wang Tingcou meant to snatch Tongjie away with a flying column, so Tongjie was beheaded and his head dispatched ahead; Cang and Jing were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚寅，加李載義同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengyin, Li Zaiyi was given the additional title of co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengyin, Li Zaiyi was made co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 諸道兵攻李同捷，三年，僅能下之。

translations.literal: The armies of the various circuits had attacked Li Tongjie for three years and only just managed to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies had fought Li Tongjie for three years before they could finally overcome him.

sentences.zh: 而柏耆徑入城，取為己功。

translations.literal: Yet Bai Qi had gone straight into the city and claimed the credit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bai Qi had ridden straight into the city and claimed the victory as his own.

sentences.zh: 諸將疾之，爭上表論列。

translations.literal: The generals resented this and vied in submitting memorials laying out the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders, outraged, flooded the court with memorials setting out what had really happened.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，貶耆為循州司戶。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Qi was demoted to revenue clerk of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Qi was demoted to revenue clerk of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 李祐尋薨。

translations.literal: Li You soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Li You died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，攝魏博副使史唐奏改名孝章。

translations.literal: On renyin, Shi Tang, acting deputy commissioner of Weibo, memorialized requesting to change his name to Xiaozhang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Shi Tang, acting Weibo deputy commissioner, asked to change his name to Xiaozhang.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙辰，詔：「鎮州四面行營各歸本道休息，但務保境，勿相往來。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingchen, an edict stated: "The expeditionary camps on all sides of Zhenzhou shall each return to their home circuits to rest; they are only to guard their borders and must not cross into one another's territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingchen, the throne ordered: "The expeditionary camps surrounding Zhenzhou shall disband to their home circuits and rest; each is to hold its own borders and keep out of the others' affairs.

sentences.zh: 惟庭湊效順，為達章表，餘皆勿受。」

translations.literal: Only Tingcou's submission of loyalty is to be forwarded in memorials; all others are not to be accepted."
translations.idiomatic: Only memorials from Tingcou affirming loyalty are to be forwarded; all others are to be rejected."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以史憲誠為兼侍中、河中節度使；

translations.literal: On xinyou, Shi Xiancheng was appointed concurrently palace attendant and military governor of Hezhong;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Shi Xiancheng was made palace attendant and military governor of Hezhong;

sentences.zh: 以李聽兼魏博節度使；

translations.literal: Li Ting was appointed concurrently military governor of Weibo;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting was made military governor of Weibo;

sentences.zh: 分相、衛、澶三州，以史孝章為節度使。

translations.literal: the three prefectures of Xiang, Wei, and Chan were separated out, and Shi Xiaozhang was made their military governor.
translations.idiomatic: the prefectures of Xiang, Wei, and Chan were carved off for Shi Xiaozhang as a separate command.

sentences.zh: 初，李祐聞柏耆殺萬洪，大驚，疾遂劇。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li You heard that Bai Qi had killed Wan Hong, he was greatly shocked and his illness grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Li You learned that Bai Qi had killed Wan Hong, he was stricken with shock and his illness turned grave.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「祐若死，是耆殺之也！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If You dies, it will be Qi who killed him!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If You dies, Qi will have killed him!"

sentences.zh: 癸酉，賜耆自盡。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Qi was granted permission to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Qi was ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使李程奏得王庭湊書，請納景州；

translations.literal: Li Cheng, military governor of Hedong, memorialized that he had received a letter from Wang Tingcou requesting to surrender Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng of Hedong reported a letter from Wang Tingcou offering to surrender Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 又奏亓志紹自縊。

translations.literal: he also memorialized that Qi Zhishao had hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: he also reported that Qi Zhishao had hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使賜史憲誠旌節，癸酉，至魏州。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to bestow the command baton and banner on Shi Xiancheng; on guiyou, it reached Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent an envoy with the command baton and banner for Shi Xiancheng; on guiyou it reached Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 時李聽自貝州還軍館陶，遷延未進，憲誠竭府庫以治行，將士怒。

translations.literal: At this time Li Ting had returned his army from Beizhou to Guantao and delayed advancing; Xiancheng drained the treasury to prepare his departure, and the officers and soldiers were enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting had withdrawn from Beizhou to Guantao and lingered there without advancing, while Xiancheng emptied the treasury to finance his move to a new post, enraging the troops.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，軍亂，殺憲誠，奉牙內都知兵馬使靈武何進滔知留後。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the army mutinied, killed Xiancheng, and installed He Jintao of Lingwu, commander of the inner guard, as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the troops mutinied, killed Xiancheng, and set up He Jintao of Lingwu, the inner-guard commander, as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 李聽進至魏州，進滔拒之，不得入。

translations.literal: Li Ting advanced to Weizhou; Jintao barred him and he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting marched to Weizhou, but Jintao refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，進滔出兵擊李聽。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Jintao sent out troops to attack Li Ting.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Jintao took the field against Li Ting.

sentences.zh: 聽不為備，大敗，潰走，晝夜兼行，趣淺口，失亡過半，輜重兵械盡棄之。

translations.literal: Ting was unprepared, suffered a great defeat, and fled in rout, traveling day and night without rest toward Qiankou; more than half his force was lost, and baggage, supplies, and weapons were all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Caught unprepared, Ting was routed and fled day and night toward Qiankou, losing more than half his men and abandoning all baggage and arms.

sentences.zh: 昭義兵救之，聽僅而得免，歸於滑台。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi troops rescued him; Ting barely escaped and returned to Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi troops rescued him, and Ting barely escaped with his life, retreating to Huatai.

sentences.zh: 河北久用兵，饋運不給，朝廷厭苦之。

translations.literal: Hebei had seen warfare for a long time; supply transport could not keep up, and the court was weary of the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei had been at war for years, supplies could not keep pace, and the court was exhausted by the effort.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬子，以進滔為魏博節度使，復以相、衛、澶三州歸之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renzi, Jintao was appointed military governor of Weibo, and the three prefectures of Xiang, Wei, and Chan were returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renzi, Jintao was confirmed as Weibo governor and given back Xiang, Wei, and Chan.

sentences.zh: 滄州承喪亂之餘，骸骨蔽地，城空野曠，戶口存者什無三四，癸丑，以衛尉卿殷侑為齊、德、滄、景節度使。

translations.literal: Cangzhou, in the aftermath of war and disorder, had bones covering the ground; the cities were empty and the fields desolate, and only three or four households in ten remained. On guichou, Yin You, minister of the guard, was appointed military governor of Qi, De, Cang, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou lay in ruins after the rebellion—bones littered the ground, towns stood empty, and barely three or four households in ten had survived. On guichou, Yin You, minister of the guard, was sent to govern Qi, De, Cang, and Jing.

sentences.zh: 侑至鎮，與士卒同甘苦，招撫百姓，勸之耕桑，流散者稍稍復業。

translations.literal: When You reached his post, he shared hardship with the soldiers, comforted and settled the people, urged them to farm and raise silkworms, and the displaced gradually returned to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his command, You shared the soldiers' hardships, reassured the populace, urged farming and sericulture, and refugees slowly returned to their fields.

sentences.zh: 先是，本軍三萬人皆仰給度支，侑至一年，租稅自能贍其半；

translations.literal: Previously, the thirty thousand troops of the command had all depended on the Department of Public Works for supplies; within a year of You's arrival, local taxes and levies could support half of them;
translations.idiomatic: Previously all thirty thousand troops had been fed from the central treasury; within a year under You, local taxes covered half their needs;

sentences.zh: 二年，請悉罷度支給賜；

translations.literal: in the second year he requested that all grants from the Department of Public Works be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: in the second year he asked that central subsidies be cut off entirely;

sentences.zh: 三年之後，戶口滋殖，倉廩充盈。

translations.literal: after three years the population multiplied and the granaries were full.
translations.idiomatic: within three years the population had grown again and the granaries were full.

sentences.zh: 王庭水奏因鄰道微露請服之意。

translations.literal: Wang Tingshui memorialized that through a neighboring circuit he had subtly revealed an intention to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingshui reported that, through a neighboring circuit, he had hinted at a wish to submit.

sentences.zh: 壬申，赦庭水奏及將士，復其官爵。

translations.literal: On renshen, Tingshui's memorial and his officers and soldiers were pardoned, and their ranks and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Tingshui and his troops were pardoned and their offices and titles restored.

sentences.zh: 征浙西觀察使李德裕為兵部侍郎，裴度薦以為相。

translations.literal: Li Deyu, observation commissioner of Zhexi, was summoned to be vice minister of war; Pei Du recommended him for chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu, governor of Zhexi, was recalled as vice minister of war; Pei Du urged making him chancellor.

sentences.zh: 會吏部侍郎李宗閔有宦官之助，甲戌，以宗閔同平章事。

translations.literal: But Vice Minister of Personnel Li Zongmin had the eunuchs' support; on jiaxu, Zongmin was appointed co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Zongmin of the Ministry of Personnel had eunuch backing, and on jiaxu he was made co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery instead.

sentences.zh: 上性儉素、九月，辛巳，命中尉以下毋得衣紗縠綾羅。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature frugal and plain. In the ninth month, on xinsi, he ordered that from the commandant of the palace armies downward no one might wear gauze, damask, silk, or brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was naturally austere. In the ninth month, on xinsi, he forbade the commandant of the palace armies and all ranks below to wear gauze, damask, silk, or brocade.

sentences.zh: 聽朝之暇，惟以書史自娛，聲樂游畋未嘗留意。

translations.literal: In his leisure from court audiences he amused himself only with books and histories; music, pleasure, and hunting never held his attention.
translations.idiomatic: In his hours away from court he read history for pleasure and never troubled himself with music, feasting, or the hunt.

sentences.zh: 附馬韋處仁嘗著夾羅巾，上謂曰：「朕慕卿門地清素，故有選尚。

translations.literal: The imperial son-in-law Wei Churen once wore a double-layer gauze turban; the emperor said to him: "I admired your family's reputation for purity and simplicity, and therefore chose you for marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son-in-law Wei Churen once wore a layered gauze cap; the emperor told him, "I chose you for marriage because your family is known for plain living.

sentences.zh: 如此巾服，聽其他貴戚為之，卿不須爾。」

translations.literal: Such headgear and dress may be left to other noble kin; you need not do likewise."
translations.idiomatic: Let other nobles dress like that; you need not."

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以李德裕為義成節度使。

translations.literal: On renchen, Li Deyu was appointed military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Li Deyu was sent out as military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔惡其逼己，故出之。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin hated him for pressing too close and therefore had him sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin resented his rivalry and had him posted away from court.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙辰，以李聽為太子少師。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingchen, Li Ting was appointed junior tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingchen, Li Ting was made junior tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 路隋言於上曰：「宰相任重，不宜兼金谷瑣碎之務，如楊國忠、元載、皇甫鎛皆奸臣，所為不足法也。」

translations.literal: Lu Sui said to the emperor: "The chancellors bear heavy responsibility and should not also take on petty fiscal duties; men such as Yang Guozhong, Yuan Zai, and Huangfu Bo were all treacherous ministers whose conduct is not fit to be imitated."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui told the emperor, "Chancellors carry weighty duties and should not also handle petty treasury affairs. Yang Guozhong, Yuan Zai, and Huangfu Bo were all corrupt ministers—no model to follow."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是裴度辭度支，上許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pei Du resigned from the Department of Public Works, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du then resigned from the treasury portfolio, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲午，上祀圓丘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiawu, the emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiawu, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: He proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 四方毋得獻奇巧之物，其纖麗布帛皆禁之，焚其機杼。

translations.literal: The four quarters were forbidden to present curious and ingenious objects; all fine and ornate cloth was banned, and the looms that produced it were burned.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces were forbidden to send curios or ingenious novelties; fine and ornate textiles were banned and the looms that wove them were burned.

sentences.zh: 丙申，西川節度使杜元穎奏南詔入寇。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Du Yuanying, military governor of Xichuan, memorialized that Nanzhao had invaded.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Du Yuanying of Xichuan reported a Nanzhao invasion.

sentences.zh: 元穎以舊相，文雅自高，不曉軍事，專務蓄積，減削士卒衣糧。

translations.literal: Yuanying, as a former chancellor, prided himself on literary refinement, understood nothing of military affairs, devoted himself solely to accumulation, and cut the soldiers' clothing and rations.
translations.idiomatic: A former chancellor, Yuanying prided himself on culture, knew nothing of war, hoarded wealth, and pared the troops' clothing and rations.

sentences.zh: 西南戍邊之卒，衣食不足，皆入蠻境鈔盜以自給，蠻人反以衣食資之。

translations.literal: The garrison troops on the southwestern frontier, lacking food and clothing, all crossed into barbarian territory to raid for their livelihood, and the barbarians in turn supplied them with food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrisons in the southwest, short of food and clothing, raided across the border to survive, and the barbarians supplied them in return.

sentences.zh: 由是蜀中虛實動靜，蠻皆知之。

translations.literal: Thus the strengths and weaknesses and every movement in Shu were known to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the barbarians knew Shu’s strengths, weaknesses, and every move.

sentences.zh: 南詔自嵯顛謀大舉入寇，邊州屢以告，元穎不之信。

translations.literal: Nanzhao under Cuan Dian planned a major invasion; the border prefectures repeatedly reported it, but Yuanying would not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Cuan Dian, Nanzhao planned a major invasion; border posts warned again and again, but Yuanying refused to believe them.

sentences.zh: 嵯顛兵至，邊城一無備御。

translations.literal: When Cuan Dian's army arrived, the border cities had no defenses whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: When Cuan Dian's army arrived, the border towns had no defenses at all.

sentences.zh: 蠻以蜀卒為鄉導，襲陷巂、戎二州。

translations.literal: The barbarians used Shu soldiers as guides and stormed and captured Xi and Rong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Using Shu soldiers as guides, they stormed and took Xi and Rong.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，元穎遣兵與戰於邛州南，蜀兵大敗，蠻遂陷邛州。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Yuanying sent troops to give battle south of Qiongzhou; the Shu army was greatly defeated, and the barbarians then captured Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Yuanying sent troops to fight south of Qiongzhou; the Shu army was routed and the barbarians took the city.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使王智興入朝。

translations.literal: Wang Zhixing, military governor of Wuning, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing of Wuning came to court.

sentences.zh: 詔發東川、興元、荊南兵以救西川。

translations.literal: An edict ordered troops from Dongchuan, Xingyuan, and Jingnan to be mobilized to rescue Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from Dongchuan, Xingyuan, and Jingnan were ordered to relieve Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁未朔，又發鄂岳、襄鄧、陳許等兵繼之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day dingwei, troops from E-Yue, Xiang-Deng, Chen-Xu, and other commands were sent in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day dingwei, forces from E-Yue, Xiang-Deng, Chen-Xu, and other circuits followed.

sentences.zh: 以王智興為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Zhixing was appointed military governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing was made military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以東川節度使郭釗為西川節度使，兼權東川節度事。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Guo Zhao, military governor of Dongchuan, was appointed military governor of Xichuan and given concurrent charge of Dongchuan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Guo Zhao of Dongchuan was made governor of Xichuan and given interim authority over Dongchuan as well.

sentences.zh: 嵯顛自邛州引兵徑抵成都。

translations.literal: Cuan Dian led his army from Qiongzhou straight to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Cuan Dian marched from Qiongzhou straight on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，陷其外郭。

translations.literal: On gengxu, he captured the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu he took the outer city.

sentences.zh: 杜元穎帥眾保牙城以拒之，欲遁去者數四。

translations.literal: Du Yuanying led the masses to hold the inner citadel in defense; four times he wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanying held the inner citadel with his troops but four times tried to flee.

sentences.zh: 壬子，貶元穎為邵州刺史。

translations.literal: On renzi, Yuanying was demoted to prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Yuanying was demoted to prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 己未，以右領軍大將軍董重質為神策、諸道西川行營節度使，又發太原、鳳翔兵赴西川。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Dong Chongzhi, great general of the Right Army of the Right Wing, was appointed military governor of the Shence and multi-circuit Xichuan expeditionary camp; troops from Taiyuan and Fengxiang were also sent to Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Dong Chongzhi was made commander of the Shence and allied Xichuan expedition, and troops from Taiyuan and Fengxiang were dispatched west.

sentences.zh: 南詔寇東川，入梓州西郭。

translations.literal: Nanzhao raided Dongchuan and entered the western suburbs of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao raided Dongchuan and entered the western suburbs of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 郭釗兵寡弱不能戰，以書責嵯顛。

translations.literal: Guo Zhao's forces were few and weak and could not fight; he sent a letter reproaching Cuan Dian.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhao's force was too small to fight; he sent Cuan Dian a letter of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 嵯顛覆書曰：「杜元穎侵擾我，故興兵報之耳。」

translations.literal: Cuan Dian replied in a letter: "Du Yuanying harassed us, and therefore I raised troops to repay him."
translations.idiomatic: Cuan Dian wrote back, "Du Yuanying provoked us—that is why I took the field."

sentences.zh: 與釗修好而退。

translations.literal: He made peace with Zhao and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He made peace with Guo Zhao and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蠻留成都西郭十日，其始慰撫蜀人，市肆立堵。

translations.literal: The barbarians remained in the western suburbs of Chengdu for ten days; at first they comforted the people of Shu and the market stalls stood intact.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians camped in Chengdu's western suburbs for ten days; at first they reassured the populace and the markets still stood.

sentences.zh: 將行，乃大掠子女、百工數萬人及珍貨而去。

translations.literal: When they were about to depart, they carried out a great plunder of women and children, several tens of thousands of artisans, and precious goods, and left.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to leave, they seized women and children, tens of thousands of craftsmen, and hoards of treasure.

sentences.zh: 蜀人恐懼，往往赴江，流屍塞江而下。

translations.literal: The people of Shu, in terror, often threw themselves into the river; corpses floated down and choked the current.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified Shu subjects threw themselves into the rivers until the waters were choked with corpses downstream.

sentences.zh: 嵯顛自為軍殿，及大度水，嵯顛謂蜀人曰：「此南吾境也，聽汝哭別鄉國。」

translations.literal: Cuan Dian himself brought up the rear of the army; when they reached the Dadu River, Cuan Dian said to the people of Shu: "South of here is our territory; you may weep your farewell to your homeland."
translations.idiomatic: Cuan Dian brought up the rear; at the Dadu River he told the Shu captives, "Beyond here lies our land—weep your farewell to your country if you wish."

sentences.zh: 眾皆慟哭，赴水死者以千計。

translations.literal: All wept bitterly; those who drowned themselves in the water numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They wept in anguish; thousands drowned themselves in the river.

sentences.zh: 自是南詔工巧埒於蜀中。

translations.literal: From this time on, Nanzhao's craftsmanship rivaled that of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Nanzhao's craft and skill matched what Shu had possessed.

sentences.zh: 嵯顛遣使上表，稱：「蠻比修職貢，豈敢犯邊，正以杜元穎不恤軍士，怨苦元穎，競為鄉導，祈我此行以誅虐帥。

translations.literal: Cuan Dian sent an envoy to submit a memorial, stating: "Our people have faithfully paid tribute—how would we dare violate the border? It is only because Du Yuanying did not care for his soldiers; resenting and bitter against Yuanying, they competed to serve as local guides, begging for this expedition of ours to punish the cruel commander.
translations.idiomatic: Cuan Dian sent a memorial claiming, "We have always paid tribute in good faith—we would never raid your borders. Du Yuanying neglected his troops; resenting him, they vied to guide us here, asking us to punish their brutal commander.

sentences.zh: 誅之不遂，無以慰蜀士之心，願陛下誅之。」

translations.literal: If he is not executed, there is no way to comfort the hearts of the soldiers of Shu; we wish Your Majesty to execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Unless he is put to death, the soldiers of Shu cannot be pacified. We beg Your Majesty to execute him."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，再貶元穎循州司馬。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Du Yuanying was again demoted to vice prefect of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Du Yuanying was demoted once more to deputy prefect of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔董重質及諸道兵皆引還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dong Chongzhi and the troops of all circuits to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Dong Chongzhi and the allied armies to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 郭釗至成都，與南詔立約，不相侵擾。

translations.literal: Guo Zhao arrived at Chengdu and made a pact with Nanzhao not to harass each other.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhao reached Chengdu and concluded a non-aggression pact with Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 詔遣中使以國信賜嵯顛。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched an imperial envoy to bestow credentials of the state upon Cuan Dian.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent an imperial envoy to confer formal recognition upon Cuan Dian.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，武昌節度使牛僧孺入朝。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, Niu Sengru, military governor of Wuchang, entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on xinsi of the first month, Niu Sengru, governor of Wuchang, arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 戊子，立子永為魯王。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the emperor installed his son Yong as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the emperor made his son Yong Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔引薦牛僧孺。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin recommended Niu Sengru.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin put Niu Sengru forward for appointment.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以僧孺為兵部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Niu Sengru was appointed Minister of War and Associate Councilor of State.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Niu Sengru was made Minister of War and a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 於是二人相與排擯李德裕之黨，稍稍逐之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the two men together excluded the faction of Li Deyu and gradually drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: The two then joined forces to purge Li Deyu's faction, gradually forcing his allies from office.

sentences.zh: 南詔之寇成都也，詔山南西道發兵救之，興元兵少，節度使李絳募兵千人赴之，未至，蠻退而還。

translations.literal: When Nanzhao raided Chengdu, an edict ordered Shannan West Circuit to dispatch troops to the rescue; Xingyuan had few troops, and its military governor Li Jiang recruited a thousand men to march there; before they arrived, the barbarians had withdrawn and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: During Nanzhao's raid on Chengdu, the court ordered Shannan West to send relief. Xingyuan's garrison was small, so Governor Li Jiang raised a thousand men; the barbarians withdrew before they arrived.

sentences.zh: 興元兵有常額，詔新募兵悉罷之。

translations.literal: Xingyuan's army had a fixed quota; an edict ordered all newly recruited troops to be disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyuan had a standing quota; the court ordered all newly raised troops disbanded.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯，絳悉召新軍，諭以詔旨而遣之，仍賜以廩麥，皆怏怏而退。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yimao, Li Jiang summoned all the new troops, informed them of the edict and dismissed them, yet still bestowed upon them rations of grain; all withdrew discontentedly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yimao, Li Jiang assembled the new recruits, read them the dismissal order, and gave them grain rations—all left sullen and dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 往辭監軍，監軍楊叔元素惡絳不奉己，以賜物薄激之。

translations.literal: When they went to take leave of the army supervisor, the supervisor Yang Shuyuan, who disliked Li Jiang for not deferring to him, goaded them by saying the gifts were meager.
translations.idiomatic: When they went to bid farewell to Army Supervisor Yang Shuyuan, he—resentful that Li Jiang had not deferred to him—provoked them by complaining the rations were too scant.

sentences.zh: 眾怒，大噪，掠庫兵，趨使牙。

translations.literal: The crowd grew angry and raised a great clamor, plundered the armory, and rushed toward the headquarters gate.
translations.idiomatic: The men erupted in fury, raided the armory, and stormed the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 絳方與僚佐宴，不為備，走登北城。

translations.literal: Li Jiang was just then feasting with his subordinates and made no preparations; he fled and climbed the north wall.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang was at a banquet with his staff and unprepared; he fled onto the north rampart.

sentences.zh: 或勸縋而出，絳曰：「吾為元帥，豈可逃去！」

translations.literal: Someone urged him to be lowered by rope and escape; Li Jiang said: "I am the commander—how can I flee!"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to be lowered over the wall by rope. Li Jiang said, "I am the commander—how can I run away?"

sentences.zh: 麾推官趙存約令去。

translations.literal: He waved his hand and ordered Push Officer Zhao Cunyue to leave.
translations.idiomatic: He gestured for his aide Zhao Cunyue to go.

sentences.zh: 存約曰：「存約受明公知，何可苟免！」

translations.literal: Cunyue said: "Cunyue has received your lordship's trust—how can I seek to save myself alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Cunyue replied, "You have shown me favor—I cannot save myself alone."

sentences.zh: 牙將王景延與賊力戰死，絳、存約及觀察判官薛齊皆為亂兵所害，賊遂屠絳家。

translations.literal: Garrison officer Wang Jingyan fought the rebels to the death; Li Jiang, Cunyue, and administrative aide Xue Qi were all killed by the mutinous troops, and the rebels then slaughtered Li Jiang's family.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison officer Wang Jingyan fought the mutineers to the death. Li Jiang, Zhao Cunyue, and aide Xue Qi were all killed, and the rebels massacred Li Jiang's household.

sentences.zh: 戊午，叔元奏絳收新軍募直以致亂。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Shuyuan memorialized that Li Jiang had collected recruitment fees from the new troops, causing the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Yang Shuyuan reported that Li Jiang had pocketed the new recruits' enlistment pay, provoking the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以尚書右丞溫造為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Wen Zao, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed military governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Wen Zao was appointed governor of Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 是時，三省官上疏共論李絳之冤。

translations.literal: At this time, officials of the Three Departments jointly submitted memorials discussing Li Jiang's wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Three Departments jointly memorialized the throne, arguing that Li Jiang had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫憶敏行具孫叔元激怒亂兵，上始悟。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Counsellor Wei Minxing detailed how Yang Shuyuan had provoked the mutinous troops; the emperor at last understood.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counsellor Wei Minxing laid out how Yang Shuyuan had incited the mutineers, and the emperor finally saw the truth.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙亥朔，以刑部尚書柳公綽為河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day yihai, Liu Gongchuo, Minister of Justice, was appointed military governor of Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the third month, Liu Gongchuo was appointed governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 先是，回鶻入貢及互市，所過恐其為變，常嚴兵迎送防衛之。

translations.literal: Previously, when the Uighurs came to pay tribute and for mutual trade, the places they passed through, fearing they might cause trouble, always deployed strict troops to escort and guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Uighur tribute missions and trade caravans passed through, local officials fearing trouble posted heavy escorts.

sentences.zh: 公綽至鎮，回鶻遣梅錄李暢以馬萬匹互市，公綽但遣牙將單騎迎勞於境，至則大辟牙門，受其禮謁。

translations.literal: When Gongchuo arrived at his post, the Uighurs sent the meruy Li Chang with ten thousand horses for mutual trade; Gongchuo only sent a garrison officer alone on horseback to welcome and treat them at the border; when they arrived, he fully opened the headquarters gate and received their ceremonial visit.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Gongchuo took up his post, the Uighurs sent Meruy Li Chang with ten thousand horses to trade. Liu Gongchuo sent a single officer to greet them at the border; when they arrived, he threw open his headquarters and received them with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 暢感泣，戒其下，在路不敢馳獵，無所侵擾。

translations.literal: Chang wept with emotion, admonished his subordinates, and on the road dared not gallop or hunt; they committed no harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang was moved to tears and warned his men not to gallop or hunt along the route; they disturbed no one.

sentences.zh: 陘北沙陀素驍勇，為九姓、六州胡所畏伏。

translations.literal: The Shatuo north of the passes were naturally fierce and brave, and were feared and submitted to by the Nine Surnames and Six Prefectures Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo north of the passes were renowned fighters; the Nine Surnames and Six Prefectures tribes feared and obeyed them.

sentences.zh: 公綽奏以其酋長朱邪執宜為陰山都督、代北行營招撫使，使居雲、朔塞下，捍御北邊。

translations.literal: Gongchuo memorialized that their chieftain Zhuye Zhiyi be made governor of Yinshan and pacification commissioner of the Daibei field camp, to reside below the passes of Yun and Shuo and defend the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongchuo recommended their chieftain Zhuye Zhiyi as Yinshan governor and frontier pacification commissioner, stationing his people below the Yun and Shuo passes to guard the north.

sentences.zh: 執宜與諸酋長入謁，公綽與之宴。

translations.literal: Zhiyi and the other chieftains came to audience; Gongchuo feasted with them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuye Zhiyi and the other chiefs paid their respects; Liu Gongchuo hosted a banquet for them.

sentences.zh: 執宜神彩嚴整，進退有禮。

translations.literal: Zhiyi's bearing was stern and dignified; in advancing and withdrawing he observed propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuye Zhiyi bore himself with stern dignity and perfect courtesy.

sentences.zh: 公綽謂僚佐曰：「執宜外嚴而內寬，言徐而理當，福祿人也。」

translations.literal: Gongchuo said to his aides: "Zhiyi is stern outwardly yet generous within; his speech is measured and his reasoning sound—a man destined for fortune and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongchuo told his staff, "Zhuye Zhiyi looks stern but is generous at heart; he speaks slowly and to the point—a man marked for high fortune."

sentences.zh: 執宜母妻入見，公綽使夫人與之飲酒，饋遺之。

translations.literal: Zhiyi's mother and wife came to audience; Gongchuo had his wife drink wine with them and sent them gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuye Zhiyi's mother and wife were presented, Liu Gongchuo had his own wife share wine with them and sent gifts.

sentences.zh: 執宜感恩，為之盡力。

translations.literal: Zhiyi, grateful, exerted himself to the utmost on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful, Zhuye Zhiyi served him with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 塞下舊有廢府十一，執宜修之，使其部落三千人分守之，自是雜虜不敢犯塞。

translations.literal: Below the passes there had formerly been eleven abandoned forts; Zhiyi restored them and had three thousand men of his tribe garrison them in rotation; from this time mixed barbarians did not dare violate the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven abandoned forts lay below the passes; Zhuye Zhiyi repaired them and posted three thousand tribesmen to hold them. Thereafter no raiders dared cross the frontier.

sentences.zh: 溫造行至褒城，遇興元都將衛志忠征蠻歸，造密與之謀誅亂者，以其兵八百人為牙隊，五百人為前軍，入府，分守諸門。

translations.literal: Wen Zao reached Baocheng and encountered Xingyuan capital guard commander Wei Zhizhong returning from campaigning against the barbarians; Zao secretly plotted with him to execute the mutineers, taking his eight hundred men as the headquarters guard corps and five hundred as the vanguard; they entered the headquarters and posted guards at every gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Baocheng, Wen Zao met Wei Zhizhong returning from a campaign against the barbarians. They secretly planned to crush the mutineers, deploying Wei's eight hundred men as headquarters guards and five hundred as a vanguard; they entered the compound and sealed every gate.

sentences.zh: 己卯，造視事，饗將士於牙門，造曰：「吾欲問新軍去留之意，宜悉使來前。」

translations.literal: On jimao, Zao assumed office and feasted the officers and men at the headquarters gate; Zao said: "I wish to inquire of the new troops their intent regarding staying or leaving; they should all be brought forward."
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Wen Zao took office and hosted the garrison at headquarters. "I want to hear the new troops' wishes on staying or leaving," he said. "Bring them all forward."

sentences.zh: 既勞問，命坐，行酒。

translations.literal: After expressing his solicitude and inquiry, he ordered them seated and wine served.
translations.idiomatic: After greeting them, he had them sit and wine circulated.

sentences.zh: 志忠密以牙兵圍之，既合，唱「殺！」

translations.literal: Zhizhong secretly had the headquarters guard surround them; when closed in, he shouted "Kill!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhizhong's guards closed the ring; at the signal he roared, "Kill them!"

sentences.zh: 新軍八百餘人皆死。

translations.literal: More than eight hundred of the new troops all died.
translations.idiomatic: More than eight hundred new recruits were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 楊叔元起，擁造靴求生，造命囚之。

translations.literal: Yang Shuyuan rose up, embraced Wen Zao's boots and begged for his life; Zao ordered him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shuyuan clutched Wen Zao's boots and begged for mercy; Wen Zao had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 其手殺絳者，斬之百段，餘皆斬首，投屍漢水，以百首祭李絳，三十首祭死事者，具事以聞。

translations.literal: Those who had personally killed Li Jiang were chopped into a hundred pieces; the rest were all beheaded, their corpses cast into the Han River; a hundred heads were used to sacrifice to Li Jiang and thirty heads to sacrifice to those who died in service; the full account was reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had killed Li Jiang with their own hands were hacked into pieces; the rest were beheaded and their bodies thrown into the Han. A hundred heads were offered in Li Jiang's memory and thirty for the other dead; Wen Zao reported all to court.

sentences.zh: 己丑，流楊叔元於康州。

translations.literal: On jichou, Yang Shuyuan was banished to Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Yang Shuyuan was exiled to Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，加淮南節度使段文昌同平章事、為荊南節度使。

translations.literal: On guimao, Duan Wenchang, military governor of Huainan, was additionally made Associate Councilor of State and appointed military governor of Jingnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Duan Wenchang of Huainan was made a chief minister and transferred to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 奚寇幽州。

translations.literal: The Xi raided Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi attacked Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁未，盧龍節度使李載義擊破之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingwei, Li Zaiyi, military governor of Lulong, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingwei, Li Zaiyi of Lulong routed them.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，擒其王茹羯以獻。

translations.literal: On xinyou, he captured their king Rujie and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, he captured the Xi king Rujie and sent him to court.

sentences.zh: 裴度以高年多疾，懇辭機政。

translations.literal: Pei Du, advanced in years and afflicted with illness, earnestly declined active governance.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du, aged and ill, begged to be relieved of daily governance.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁未，以度為司徒、平章軍國重事，俟疾損，三五日一入中書。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingwei, Du was made Grand Mentor and Grand Councilor of State Affairs; when his illness lessened, he was to enter the Secretariat once every three or five days.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingwei, Pei Du was made Grand Mentor with oversight of state affairs, entering the Secretariat only every few days as his health allowed.

sentences.zh: 上患宦官強盛，憲宗、敬宗弒逆之黨猶有在左右者。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled that the eunuchs were powerful; adherents of the regicides of Emperor Xianzong and Emperor Jingzong still remained at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried over eunuch power; men linked to the murders of Emperors Xianzong and Jingzong still surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 中尉王守澄尤為專橫，招權納賄，上不能制。

translations.literal: Commandant Wang Shoucheng was especially domineering, gathering power and accepting bribes; the emperor could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Wang Shoucheng was especially overbearing, trading on power and taking bribes beyond the emperor's control.

sentences.zh: 嘗密與翰林學士宋申錫言之，申錫請漸除其逼。

translations.literal: The emperor once secretly spoke of this with Hanlin Academician Song Shenxi; Shenxi asked to gradually remove their pressure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confided in Hanlin scholar Song Shenxi, who proposed whittling away their grip step by step.

sentences.zh: 上以申錫沉厚忠謹，可倚以事，擢為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Shenxi steady, loyal, and careful, trustworthy for such affairs, and promoted him to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting Song Shenxi's steadiness and loyalty, the emperor promoted him to vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未，以申錫同平章事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiwei, Shenxi was made Associate Councilor of State.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on guiwei of the seventh month, Song Shenxi was made a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 初，裴度征淮西，奏李宗閔為觀察判官，由是漸獲進用。

translations.literal: Initially, when Pei Du campaigned against Huai Xi, he recommended Li Zongmin as administrative aide, and from this he gradually gained advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du campaigned in Huai Xi, he had recommended Li Zongmin as his aide; from that Li Zongmin rose by degrees.

sentences.zh: 至是，怨度薦李德裕，因其謝病，九月，壬午，以度兼侍中，充山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: At this time, resenting that Du had recommended Li Deyu, and taking advantage of his request for sick leave, in the ninth month, on renwu, Du was additionally made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and appointed military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Now resenting Pei Du for backing Li Deyu, Li Zongmin used Pei's illness as pretext; in the ninth month, on renwu, Pei Du was made vice director and sent to govern Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使郭釗以疾求代，冬，十月，戊申，以義成節度使李德裕為西川節度使。

translations.literal: Guo Zhao, military governor of Xichuan, requested replacement on account of illness; in winter, the tenth month, on wushen, Li Deyu, military governor of Yicheng, was appointed military governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhao of Xichuan sought relief for illness; in winter, on wushen of the tenth month, Li Deyu was transferred from Yicheng to Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 蜀自南詔入寇，一方殘弊，郭釗多病，未暇完補。

translations.literal: Since Nanzhao's invasion, Shu had been devastated throughout the region; Guo Zhao was often ill and had no leisure to repair and restore.
translations.idiomatic: Since Nanzhao's invasion Shu lay in ruins; Guo Zhao had been too ill to rebuild.

sentences.zh: 德裕至鎮，作籌邊樓，圖蜀地形，南入南詔，西達吐蕃。

translations.literal: When Deyu arrived at his post, he built the Frontier Planning Tower and mapped the terrain of Shu, south into Nanzhao and west to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu built a Frontier Planning Tower and mapped Shu from the Nanzhao border to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 日召老於軍旅、習邊事者，雖走卒蠻夷無所間，訪以山川、城邑、道路險易廣狹遠近，未逾月，皆若身嘗涉歷。

translations.literal: Daily he summoned those long in military service and versed in frontier affairs—even runners and barbarians without distinction—and inquired about mountains and rivers, cities and towns, roads and their difficulty, width, narrowness, distance, and nearness; within a month he knew them all as if he had personally traversed them.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned anyone with frontier experience—runners and tribesmen alike—about terrain, towns, and roads. Within a month he knew the land as if he had marched every mile.

sentences.zh: 上命德裕修塞清溪關以斷南詔入寇之路，或無土，則以石壘之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Deyu to repair and block Qingxi Pass to cut off Nanzhao's route of invasion; where there was no earth, stone was to be piled up.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Li Deyu to fortify Qingxi Pass and block Nanzhao's invasion route, piling stone where earth was lacking.

sentences.zh: 德裕上言：「通蠻細路至多，不可塞，惟重兵鎮守，可保無虞。

translations.literal: Deyu submitted a memorial: "Paths leading to the barbarians are too numerous to block; only by garrisoning with heavy troops can we ensure no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu replied, "Too many paths lead to the barbarians to seal them all; only strong garrisons can keep the frontier safe.

sentences.zh: 但黎、雅以來得萬人，成都得二萬人，精加訓練，則蠻不敢動矣。

translations.literal: If from Li and Ya onward there were ten thousand men, and at Chengdu twenty thousand, rigorously trained, then the barbarians would not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand men from Li and Ya southward and twenty thousand at Chengdu, properly trained, would keep the barbarians still.

sentences.zh: 邊兵又不宜多，須力可臨制。

translations.literal: Frontier troops moreover should not be too many; their strength must be such that they can be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrisons must not be too large—they must remain forces the court can control.

sentences.zh: 崔旰之殺郭英乂，張朏之逐張延賞，皆鎮兵也。」

translations.literal: Cui Gan's killing of Guo Yingyi and Zhang Fei's expulsion of Zhang Yanshang were both done by garrison troops."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gan murdered Guo Yingyi and Zhang Fei drove out Zhang Yanshang—both acts of mutinous garrison troops."

sentences.zh: 時北兵皆歸本道，惟河中、陳許三千人在成都，有詔來年三月亦歸，蜀人朏懼。

translations.literal: At this time northern troops all returned to their home circuits; only three thousand from Hezhong and Chenxu remained at Chengdu; there was an edict that next year in the third month they too would return; the people of Shu were all alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops were returning home; only three thousand from Hezhong and Chenxu remained in Chengdu, with orders to leave the following March. The people of Shu were terrified.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏乞鄭滑五百人、陳許千人以鎮蜀。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized requesting five hundred men from Zheng-Hua and a thousand from Chenxu to garrison Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu asked for five hundred men from Zheng-Hua and a thousand from Chenxu to hold Shu.

sentences.zh: 且言：「蜀兵脆弱，新為蠻寇所困，皆破膽，不堪征戌。

translations.literal: He further stated: "Shu troops are weak and fragile; newly harried by barbarian raiders, all have lost their courage and cannot bear campaigning and garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Shu soldiers are soft—fresh from the barbarian raid, they are too shaken for field service.

sentences.zh: 若北兵盡歸，則與杜元穎時無異，蜀不可保。

translations.literal: If northern troops all return, it will be no different from Du Yuanying's time; Shu cannot be secured.
translations.idiomatic: If the northern garrisons leave entirely, Shu will be as undefended as under Du Yuanying—and will not hold.

sentences.zh: 恐議者雲蜀經蠻寇以來，已自增兵，向者蠻寇已逼，元穎始捕市人為兵，得三千餘人，徒有其數，實不可用。

translations.literal: He feared that critics would say that since the barbarian raid Shu had already increased its troops on its own; earlier, when the barbarian raid had already pressed close, Yuanying only then pressed townsmen into service as soldiers, obtaining a little more than three thousand men—they had the numbers only, and in reality could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Critics might say Shu had already raised troops after the raid—but when the barbarians were at the gates, Yuanying had merely press-ganged townsfolk into three thousand useless men.

sentences.zh: 郭釗募北兵僅得百餘人，臣復召募得二百餘人，此外皆元穎舊兵也。

translations.literal: Guo Zhao recruited northern troops and obtained barely more than a hundred men; I have again recruited and obtained more than two hundred; beyond this all are Yuanying's old troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhao raised barely a hundred northern troops; I have added barely two hundred more—all the rest are Yuanying's old soldiers.

sentences.zh: 恐議者又聞一夫當關之說，以為清溪可塞。

translations.literal: He feared critics would again hear the saying of one man holding the pass and think Qingxi could be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Others may cite the old maxim about one man holding a pass and insist Qingxi can be sealed.

sentences.zh: 臣訪之蜀中老將，清溪之旁，大路有三，自餘小徑無數，皆東蠻臨時為之開通，若言可塞，則是欺罔朝廷。

translations.literal: I inquired of old generals in Shu: beside Qingxi there are three main roads, and besides these countless small paths, all opened temporarily by the eastern barbarians; if one says they can be blocked, that is deceiving the court.
translations.idiomatic: Shu veterans tell me three main roads and countless trails run beside Qingxi—the eastern tribes open new paths at will. To claim they can all be blocked is to deceive the court.

sentences.zh: 要須大度水北更築一城，迤邐接黎州，以大兵守之方可。

translations.literal: It is essential to build another city north of the Dadu River, extending in sequence to connect with Lizhou, and only then garrison it with a large force.
translations.idiomatic: We must build a new fortress north of the Dadu River, linking it chain-fashion to Lizhou, and hold it with a substantial garrison.

sentences.zh: 況聞南詔以所掠蜀人二千及金帛賂遺吐蕃，若使二虜知蜀虛實，連兵入寇，誠可深憂。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear that Nanzhao has bribed Tibet with two thousand Shu people it captured and gold and silk; if the two barbarians learn Shu's true condition and join forces to invade, that would truly be deeply worrying.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear Nanzhao has bribed Tibet with two thousand Shu captives and treasure. If both enemies learn how weak Shu is and attack together, the danger is grave.

sentences.zh: 其朝臣建言者，蓋由禍不在身，望人責一狀，留入堂案，他日敗事，不可令臣獨當國憲。」

translations.literal: Those court ministers who offer advice do so presumably because calamity is not upon themselves; they hope others will sign a written pledge, leave it in the office files, and if affairs fail someday, I alone must not bear the nation's punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who urge easy fixes do so because the cost will not fall on them. I ask that their recommendations be signed and filed—so if disaster follows, I alone will not answer for it."

sentences.zh: 朝廷皆從其請。

translations.literal: The court accepted all his requests.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted all his requests.

sentences.zh: 德裕乃練士卒，葺堡鄣，積糧儲以備邊，蜀人粗安。

translations.literal: Deyu then trained soldiers, repaired fortifications and barriers, and stockpiled grain to prepare the frontier; the people of Shu were roughly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu drilled his troops, repaired the fortifications, and laid up supplies. Shu settled somewhat.

sentences.zh: 是歲，勃海宣王仁秀卒，子新德早死，孫彝震立，改元鹹和。

translations.literal: This year, King Renxiu of Bohai died; his son Xinde had died early; his grandson Yizhen succeeded and changed the era name to Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: That year King Renxiu of Bohai died. His son Xinde had predeceased him; grandson Yizhen succeeded and proclaimed the Xianhe era.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁巳，賜滄、齊、德節度名義昌軍。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingsi, the Cang-Qi-De military governorship was granted the name Yichang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on dingsi of the first month, the Cang-Qi-De governorship was renamed the Yichang Army.

sentences.zh: 庚申，盧龍監軍奏李載義與敕使宴於球場後院，副兵馬使楊志誠與其徒呼噪作亂，載義與子正元奔易州。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Lulong army supervisor reported that Li Zaiyi was feasting with the imperial envoy in the rear court of the ball ground when Vice commander of horse and foot Yang Zhicheng and his followers raised a clamor and mutinied; Zaiyi and his son Zhengyuan fled to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Lulong's army supervisor reported that while Li Zaiyi feasted with an imperial envoy in the ball-court rear yard, Vice commander Yang Zhicheng and his men mutinied. Zaiyi and his son Zhengyuan fled to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 志誠又殺莫州刺史張慶初。

translations.literal: Zhicheng also killed Mo Prefecture governor Zhang Qingchu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng also murdered Zhang Qingchu, governor of Mo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上召宰相謀之，牛僧孺曰：「范陽自安、史以來，非國所有，劉總暫獻其地，朝廷費錢八十萬緡而無絲毫所獲。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate; Niu Sengru said: "Fanyang since the An Lushan rebellion has not truly belonged to the state; Liu Zong temporarily surrendered its territory; the court spent eight hundred thousand strings of cash and gained not the slightest benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his chief ministers. Niu Sengru said, "Fanyang has never truly been ours since the An-Shi rebellion. Liu Zong briefly surrendered it; the court spent eight hundred thousand strings of cash and gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 今日誌誠得之，猶前日載義得之也。

translations.literal: Today Zhicheng obtains it just as yesterday Zaiyi obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicheng holds it now just as Zaiyi held it before.

sentences.zh: 因而撫之，使捍北狄，不必計其逆順。」

translations.literal: We should therefore placate him and have him repel the northern barbarians; there is no need to reckon his loyalty or rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Pacify him and set him to guard the northern frontier—we need not weigh his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 載義自易州赴京師，上以載義有平滄景之功，且事朝廷恭順，二月，壬辰，以載義為太保，同平章事如故。

translations.literal: Zaiyi came from Yizhou to the capital; the emperor, because Zaiyi had merit in pacifying Cang-Jing and moreover served the court with respectful compliance, in the second month, on renchen, made Zaiyi Grand Guardian, retaining his position as Associate Councilor of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Zaiyi reached the capital from Yizhou, the emperor—honoring his victory at Cang-Jing and his dutiful service—made him Grand Guardian while keeping him chief minister, on renchen of the second month.

sentences.zh: 以楊志誠為盧龍留後。

translations.literal: Yang Zhicheng was made acting governor of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhicheng was installed as acting governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「昔者聖人順天理，察人情，知齊民之莫能相治也，故置師長以正之；

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: "Of old the sage, following Heaven's principle and discerning human sentiment, knew that the common people cannot govern one another; therefore he set up leaders to correct them;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: "The sages, reading Heaven's order and human nature, knew the people cannot govern themselves—so they appointed leaders to set things right;

sentences.zh: 知群臣之莫能相使也，故建諸侯以制之；

translations.literal: Knowing that ministers cannot command one another, he therefore established feudal lords to restrain them;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing ministers cannot command one another, they created feudal lords to keep them in check;

sentences.zh: 知列國之莫能相服也，故立天子以統之。

translations.literal: Knowing that the various states cannot submit to one another, he therefore established the Son of Heaven to unify them.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the states would not obey one another, they enthroned a Son of Heaven to rule them all.

sentences.zh: 天子之於萬國，能褒善而黜惡，抑強而輔弱，撫服而懲違，禁暴而誅亂，然後發號施令，而四海之內莫不率從也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven toward the myriad states, able to praise the good and dismiss the evil, restrain the strong and assist the weak, soothe the compliant and punish the recalcitrant, forbid violence and execute the mutinous—only then does he issue commands, and within the four seas none fail to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the Son of Heaven can reward virtue, punish wickedness, curb the strong, aid the weak, mollify the loyal and chastise the defiant, and suppress violence and rebellion—only then do his commands run through the realm unchallenged.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」

translations.literal: The Book of Odes says: "Strive diligently, O our king, to hold the four quarters in order."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Strive, O king, to bind the four quarters in order."

sentences.zh: 載義籓屏大臣，有功於國，無罪而志誠逐之，此天子所宜治也。

translations.literal: Zaiyi is a great minister of the frontier screen, with merit to the state; without guilt Zhicheng drove him out—this is what the Son of Heaven ought to punish.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi was a meritorious frontier minister, guilty of nothing—yet Zhicheng drove him out. That is what the throne should have punished.

sentences.zh: 若一無所問，因以其土田爵位授之，則是將帥之廢置殺生皆出於士卒之手，天子雖在上，奚為哉！

translations.literal: If without a single inquiry he thereupon grants him the land, fields, and rank, then the appointment, dismissal, and life-and-death of generals all issue from the hands of common soldiers—though the Son of Heaven sits above, of what use is he!
translations.idiomatic: If the throne asks no questions and simply grants Zhicheng the domain and title, then generals will be made and broken by mere soldiers. What then is the Son of Heaven for?

sentences.zh: 國家之有方鎮，豈專利其財賦而已乎！

translations.literal: That the state has frontier garrisons—is it only to profit from their revenue and levies!
translations.idiomatic: Were frontier garrisons established only to harvest their revenue?

sentences.zh: 如僧孺之言，姑息偷安之術耳，豈宰相佐天子御天下之道哉！」

translations.literal: As in Sengru's words, it is merely the art of indulgence and clinging to ease—is this the way of a Chancellor assisting the Son of Heaven in governing the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: Sengru's counsel is mere indulgence and timid self-preservation—is that how a Chancellor helps the Son of Heaven rule the realm?"

sentences.zh: 新羅王彥升卒，子景徽立。

translations.literal: King Yeonsung of Silla died; his son Gyeonghwi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: King Yeonsung of Silla died, and his son Gyeonghwi ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 上與宋申錫謀誅宦官，申錫引吏部侍郎王璠為京兆尹，以密旨諭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Song Shenxi plotted to execute the eunuchs; Shenxi brought in Vice Minister of Personnel Wang Fan as Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao and instructed him with a secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor and Song Shenxi plotted to destroy the eunuchs. Shenxi installed Wang Fan, Vice Minister of Personnel, as Prefect of the Capital and confided the secret plan to him.

sentences.zh: 璠洩其謀，鄭注、王守澄知之，陰為之備。

translations.literal: Fan leaked the plot; Zheng Zhu and Wang Shoucheng learned of it and secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan betrayed the plot. Zheng Zhu and Wang Shoucheng learned of it and made secret preparations.

sentences.zh: 上弟漳王湊賢，有人望，注令神策都虞候豆盧著誣告申錫謀立漳王。

translations.literal: The Emperor's younger brother, the Prince of Zhang, Cou, was virtuous and enjoyed popular esteem; Zhu had the Shence Army Chief Commandant Dou Lu Zhu falsely accuse Shenxi of plotting to install the Prince of Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's brother, the Prince of Zhang, Cou, was talented and widely admired. Zheng Zhu had Dou Lu Zhu, chief commandant of the Shence Army, accuse Song Shenxi of plotting to put Cou on the throne.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，守澄奏之，上以為信然，甚怒。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Shoucheng memorialized this; the Emperor believed it true and was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, Wang Shoucheng reported the accusation to the throne. The Emperor believed it and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 守澄欲即遣二百騎屠申錫家，飛龍使馬存亮固爭曰：「如此，則京城自亂矣！

translations.literal: Shoucheng wished immediately to dispatch two hundred horsemen to slaughter Shenxi's household; the Flying Dragon Commissioner Ma Cunliang firmly remonstrated, saying: "If it were thus, the capital would fall into chaos on its own!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng wanted to send two hundred cavalry at once to massacre Song Shenxi's household. The Flying Dragon Commissioner Ma Cunliang protested fiercely: "That would throw the capital into chaos!

sentences.zh: 宜召他相與議其事。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to summon the other chancellors to discuss this matter."
translations.idiomatic: You should summon the other chancellors to discuss the matter."

sentences.zh: 守澄乃止。

translations.literal: Shoucheng thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng desisted.

sentences.zh: 是日，旬休，遣中使悉召宰相至中書東門。

translations.literal: That day was the ten-day rest; the Emperor sent palace envoys to summon all the chancellors to the eastern gate of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That day was a regular day of rest. The Emperor sent palace envoys to summon every chancellor to the eastern gate of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中使曰：「所召無宋公名。」

translations.literal: The palace envoy said: "Among those summoned, Lord Song's name is not included."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy announced: "Lord Song's name is not on the summons."

sentences.zh: 申錫知獲罪，望延英，以笏叩額而退。

translations.literal: Shenxi knew he was guilty; he gazed toward the Yanying Hall, beat his forehead with his tablet, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shenxi knew he was condemned. He looked toward the Yanying Hall, struck his forehead with his official tablet, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宰相至延英，上示以守澄所奏，相顧愕眙。

translations.literal: The chancellors arrived at Yanying; the Emperor showed them Shoucheng's memorial; they looked at one another in stunned silence.
translations.idiomatic: When the chancellors reached the Yanying Hall, the Emperor showed them Wang Shoucheng's report. They stared at one another, speechless.

sentences.zh: 上命守澄捕豆盧著所告十六宅宮市品官晏敬則及申錫親事王師文等，於禁中鞫之；

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Shoucheng to arrest those denounced by Dou Lu Zhu—the Sixteen Residence palace-market officer Yan Jingze and Shenxi's personal attendant Wang Shiwen and others—and interrogate them within the palace;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Wang Shoucheng to arrest Yan Jingze, a palace-market officer of the Sixteen Residences, and Wang Shiwen, Song Shenxi's personal attendant—among others named by Dou Lu Zhu—and interrogate them within the palace.

sentences.zh: 師文亡命。

translations.literal: Shiwen fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiwen fled.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚子，申錫罷為右庶子。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day gengzi, Shenxi was dismissed and made Right Deputy to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengzi, Song Shenxi was removed from office and appointed Right Deputy to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 自宰相大臣無敢顯言其冤者，獨京兆尹崔琯、大理卿王正雅連上疏請出內獄付外廷核實，由是獄稍緩。

translations.literal: From the chancellors and great ministers, none dared openly speak of his injustice; only Metropolitan Prefect Cui Guan and Chief Judge of the High Court Wang Zhengya repeatedly submitted memorials requesting that the case be removed from the inner prison and handed to the outer court for verification—whereby the trial was somewhat delayed.
translations.idiomatic: No minister dared openly proclaim Song Shenxi's innocence. Only Prefect Cui Guan and Chief Judge Wang Zhengya repeatedly petitioned to transfer the case from the palace prison to the regular courts for review, and the trial slackened somewhat as a result.

sentences.zh: 正雅，翊之子也。

translations.literal: Zhengya was the son of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengya was the son of Wang Yi.

sentences.zh: 晏敬則等自誣服，稱申錫遣王師文達意於王，豫結異日之知。

translations.literal: Yan Jingze and the others of themselves falsely confessed, saying Shenxi had sent Wang Shiwen to convey his intent to the Prince, establishing ties for future acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture, Yan Jingze and the others falsely confessed that Song Shenxi had sent Wang Shiwen to communicate his intentions to the Prince of Zhang, laying groundwork for a future alliance.

sentences.zh: 獄成，壬寅，上悉召師保以下及台省府寺大臣面詢之。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, on the day renyin, the Emperor summoned all from the Grand Tutors downward and the great ministers of the Secretariat, Censorate, and various bureaus to question them in person.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, when the investigation was complete, the Emperor summoned tutors, imperial advisers, and senior officials from the secretariat, censorate, and ministries to question them personally.

sentences.zh: 午際，左常侍崔玄亮、給事中李固言、諫議大夫王質、補闕盧鈞、舒元褒、蔣系、裴休、韋溫等復請對於延英，乞以獄事付外覆按。

translations.literal: At midday, Left Regular Attendant Cui Xuanliang, Drafting Middleman Li Guyen, Remonstrance and Recommendation Grandee Wang Zhi, Reminder Lu Jun, Shu Yuanbao, Jiang Xi, Pei Xiu, Wei Wen, and others again requested audience at Yanying, begging that the case be handed to the outer court for reexamination.
translations.idiomatic: At midday, Cui Xuanliang, Li Guyen, Wang Zhi, Lu Jun, Shu Yuanbao, Jiang Xi, Pei Xiu, Wei Wen, and other remonstrance officials again requested an audience at the Yanying Hall, asking that the case be reheard in the regular courts.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾已與大臣議之矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I have already discussed it with the great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I have already discussed this with my ministers."

sentences.zh: 屢遣之出，不退。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent them out, but they would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly ordered them to leave, but they refused to go.

sentences.zh: 玄亮叩頭流涕曰：「殺一匹夫，猶不可不重慎，況宰相乎！」

translations.literal: Xuanliang kowtowed and wept, saying: "Even in killing a common man, one must not fail to be cautious—how much more so a Chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanliang kowtowed, weeping: "Even the execution of a common man demands the utmost caution—how much more the case of a Chancellor!"

sentences.zh: 上意稍解，曰：「當更與宰相議之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's intent eased somewhat; he said: "I shall discuss it again with the chancellors."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger softened. "I will discuss it further with the chancellors," he said."

sentences.zh: 乃復召宰相入。

translations.literal: He then again summoned the chancellors in.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the chancellors back.

sentences.zh: 牛僧孺曰：「人臣不過宰相，今申錫已為宰相，假使如所謀，復欲何求！

translations.literal: Niu Sengru said: "Among subjects one cannot surpass the Chancellor; now Shenxi is already Chancellor—even supposing the plot were as alleged, what further would he seek!
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru said, "No subject ranks above a Chancellor. Song Shenxi already holds that office. Even if the accusation were true, what more could he want?

sentences.zh: 申錫殆不至此！」

translations.literal: Shenxi would scarcely have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Shenxi would never have gone so far!"

sentences.zh: 鄭注恐覆案詐覺，乃勸守澄請止行貶黜。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu feared a reopened case would expose the fraud; he therefore urged Shoucheng to request that only demotion and exile be imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a retrial would expose the frame-up, Zheng Zhu urged Wang Shoucheng to press for demotion and exile instead.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，貶漳王湊為巢縣公，宋申錫為開州司馬。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the Prince of Zhang Cou was demoted to Duke of Chaoxian, and Song Shenxi to Militia Vice-Commissioner of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Prince Cou of Zhang was reduced to Duke of Chaoxian, and Song Shenxi was banished to serve as vice-commissioner of militia at Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 存亮即日請致仕。

translations.literal: Cunliang that same day requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Cunliang requested retirement that same day.

sentences.zh: 玄亮，磁州人；

translations.literal: Xuanliang was a man of Cizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanliang was from Cizhou;

sentences.zh: 質，通五世孫；

translations.literal: Zhi was a fifth-generation descendant of Tong;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was a fifth-generation descendant of Wang Tong;

sentences.zh: 系，乂之子；

translations.literal: Xi was the son of Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xi was the son of Jiang Yi;

sentences.zh: 元褒，江州人也。

translations.literal: Yuanbao was a man of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanbao was from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晏敬則等坐死用及流竄者數十百人，申錫竟卒於貶所。

translations.literal: Yan Jingze and others, through involvement leading to execution and exile, numbered several tens to a hundred persons; Shenxi in the end died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens or even hundreds linked to Yan Jingze were executed or exiled. Song Shenxi ultimately died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己丑，以李載義為山南西道節度使，楊志誠為幽州節度使。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jichou: Li Zaiyi was made Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, and Yang Zhicheng Military Commissioner of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jichou, Li Zaiyi was appointed military commissioner of Shannan West, and Yang Zhicheng military commissioner of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛丑，上以太廟兩室破漏，逾月不葺，罰將作監、度支判官、宗正卿俸；

translations.literal: Fifth month, day xinchou: because the two chambers of the Grand Ancestral Temple were broken and leaking and for over a month had not been repaired, the Emperor penalized the salaries of the Director of Palace Construction, the Commissioner of Revenue's deputy, and the Director of the Imperial Clan;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinchou, the Emperor fined the Director of Palace Construction, the deputy revenue commissioner, and the Director of the Imperial Clan for allowing two halls of the Imperial Ancestral Temple to leak unrepaired for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 亟命中使帥工徒，輟禁中營繕之材以葺之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered palace envoys to lead craftsmen and conscripts, halting materials for palace construction within the Forbidden City to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered palace envoys to take work crews and divert building materials from palace repairs to fix the temple.

sentences.zh: 左補闕韋溫諫，以為：「國家置百官，各有所司，苟為墮曠，宜黜其人，更擇能者代之。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Wei Wen remonstrated, holding that: "The state establishes the hundred officials, each with his charge; if there is neglect of duty, the man ought to be dismissed and a capable person chosen to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Wei Wen remonstrated: "The state assigns each official a distinct duty. Neglect should mean removal and replacement by someone capable.

sentences.zh: 今曠官者止於罰俸，而憂軫所切即委內臣，是以宗廟為陛下所私，而百官皆為虛設也。」

translations.literal: Now the negligent official receives only a salary fine, yet what urgently concerns Your Majesty is immediately entrusted to inner attendants—thus the ancestral temple becomes Your Majesty's private concern, and the hundred officials are all empty titles."
translations.idiomatic: Yet negligent officials merely lose salary, while the Emperor personally entrusts urgent repairs to eunuchs. That makes the ancestral temple Your Majesty's private affair and renders every other post meaningless."

sentences.zh: 上善其言，即追止中使，命有司葺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words, immediately recalled and stopped the palace envoys, and ordered the relevant offices to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted the advice, recalled the envoys, and ordered the proper offices to make the repairs.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，西川節度使李德裕奏遣使詣南詔索所掠百姓，得四千人而還。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Military Commissioner Li Deyu of Xichuan memorialized that he had sent envoys to Nanzhao to demand the return of seized common people, recovering four thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Li Deyu, military commissioner of Xichuan, reported that envoys sent to Nanzhao had recovered four thousand abducted civilians.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，戊寅，以陝虢觀察使崔郾為鄂岳觀察使。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day wuyin: Observation Commissioner Cui Yan of Shan-Guo was made Observation Commissioner of E-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on wuyin, Cui Yan, observation commissioner of Shan and Guo, was transferred to E-Yue.

sentences.zh: 鄂岳地囊山帶江，處百越、巴、蜀、荊、漢之會，土多群盜，剽行舟，無老幼必盡殺乃已。

translations.literal: The land of E-Yue is wrapped by mountains and girded by rivers, situated at the convergence of Baiyue, Ba, Shu, Jing, and Han; locally there are many bandit gangs who plunder boats—with neither old nor young spared until all are killed.
translations.idiomatic: E-Yue lay among mountains and rivers at the crossroads of Baiyue, Ba, Shu, Jing, and Han. Bandits abounded, robbing river traffic and slaughtering every soul aboard, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 郾至，訓卒治兵，作蒙沖追討，歲中，悉誅之。

translations.literal: When Yan arrived, he trained soldiers and organized troops, built covered assault ships and pursued them—in midyear, he executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival, Cui Yan drilled troops, built war boats, and hunted the pirates down. Within the year he had exterminated them all.

sentences.zh: 郾在陝，以寬仁為治，或經月不笞一人，乃至鄂，嚴峻刑罰。
