translations.literal: Yan in Shan practiced lenient benevolence in governance, sometimes going a month without flogging a single person; yet upon reaching E, he applied severe punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Shanzhou Cui Yan had governed with leniency, sometimes passing a month without a single flogging. In Ezhou he ruled with iron severity.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，郾曰：「陝土瘠民貧，吾撫之不暇，尚恐其驚；

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason; Yan said: "Shan's soil is barren and its people poor—I have no leisure beyond soothing them, and still fear alarming them;
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, Cui Yan replied, "Shan's land is poor and its people are impoverished. I scarce have time to comfort them, and even gentle rule may unsettle them.

sentences.zh: 鄂地險民雜，夷俗慓狡為奸，非用威刑，不能致治。

translations.literal: E's terrain is perilous and its people mixed; barbarian custom is fierce and cunning in wickedness—without harsh punishments, good order cannot be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Ezhou is rugged and its population heterogeneous; frontier peoples are bold and devious. Without stern punishment, order is impossible.

sentences.zh: 政貴知變，蓋謂此也。」

translations.literal: In government it is prized to know change—this is what is meant."
translations.idiomatic: Good governance lies in knowing when to adapt—this is what he meant."

sentences.zh: 西川節度使李德裕奏：「蜀兵羸疾老弱者，從來終身不簡，臣命立五尺五寸之度，簡去四千四百餘人，復簡募少壯者千人以慰其心。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Li Deyu of Xichuan memorialized: "Among Shu soldiers, the weak, sick, aged, and infirm have never in all history been mustered out; your servant ordered a standard of five chi five cun established, mustered out more than four thousand four hundred men, and again mustered and recruited a thousand young strong men to comfort their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu, military commissioner of Xichuan, reported: "Sichuan troops who were weak, ill, aged, or infirm had never once been discharged. I set a height standard of five chi five cun and weeded out more than forty-four hundred men, then recruited a thousand young soldiers to reassure the ranks.

sentences.zh: 所募北兵已得千五百人，與土兵參居，轉相訓習，日益精練。

translations.literal: The northern soldiers recruited have already reached one thousand five hundred men; they dwell intermixed with local troops, training one another in turn, daily growing more skilled.
translations.idiomatic: He had already recruited fifteen hundred northern soldiers, quartered them among local troops for mutual training, and the force grew daily more disciplined.

sentences.zh: 又，蜀工所作兵器，徒務華飾不堪用。

translations.literal: Moreover, weapons made by Shu craftsmen aim only at ornamental display and are unusable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, weapons made by Sichuan craftsmen were all show and no substance.

sentences.zh: 臣今取工於別道以治之，無不堅利。」

translations.literal: Your servant now takes craftsmen from other routes to manufacture them—none fail to be solid and sharp."
translations.idiomatic: I have brought in craftsmen from elsewhere to forge arms, and none fail to be sturdy and keen."

sentences.zh: 九月，吐蕃維州副使悉怛謀請降，盡帥其眾奔成都。

translations.literal: Ninth month: the Tibetan deputy commissioner of Weizhou, Sinam, requested surrender, leading all his followers in flight to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Sinam, deputy commissioner of Weizhou for Tibet, offered to surrender and led his entire force to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 德裕遣行維州刺史虞藏儉將兵入據其城。

translations.literal: Deyu sent Acting Prefect of Weizhou Yu Zangjian to lead troops in and occupy the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu sent Yu Zangjian, acting prefect of Weizhou, to occupy the city with troops.

sentences.zh: 庚申，具奏其狀，且言「欲遣生羌三千，燒十三橋，搗西戎腹心，可洗久恥，是韋皋沒身恨不能致者也！」

translations.literal: On gengshen, he fully memorialized the situation, adding: "Your servant wishes to dispatch three thousand raw Qiang, burn the Thirteen Bridges, strike at the heart of the western barbarians—able to wash away long-standing shame; this is what Wei Gao to his dying day regretted he could not achieve!"
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he memorialized in full, proposing "to send three thousand Qiang auxiliaries to burn the Thirteen Bridges and strike deep into Tibetan territory—avenging a humiliation Wei Gao had mourned to his dying day!"

sentences.zh: 事下尚書省，集百官議，皆請如德裕策。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Department of State Affairs; the hundred officials were assembled to deliberate—all requested approval of Deyu's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the Department of State Affairs. The assembled officials unanimously endorsed Li Deyu's strategy.

sentences.zh: 牛僧孺曰：「吐蕃之境，四面各萬里，失一維州，未能損其勢。

translations.literal: Niu Sengru said: "Tibet's territory extends ten thousand li on every side; to lose one Weizhou cannot diminish its power.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru argued, "Tibetan territory stretches ten thousand li in every direction. Losing Weizhou would not weaken them.

sentences.zh: 比來修好，約罷戍兵，中國御戎，守信為上。

translations.literal: Recently peace has been established, with agreement to withdraw garrison troops; in China's defense against barbarians, keeping faith comes first.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately made peace and agreed to withdraw garrisons. In dealing with frontier peoples, honor comes first.

sentences.zh: 彼若來責曰：『何事失信？』

translations.literal: If they come to reproach us, saying: 'Why break faith?'
translations.idiomatic: If they demand, 'Why have you broken faith?'

sentences.zh: 養馬蔚茹川，上平涼阪，萬騎綴回中，怒氣直辭，不三日至咸陽橋。

translations.literal: They will raise horses at Weiruchuan, ascend Pingliang Slope, ten thousand horsemen pressing toward Huizhong—with wrath in their straight speech, in fewer than three days they will reach Xianyang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: They will pasture horses on the Weiruchuan plain, cross Pingliang Pass, and ten thousand cavalry will press toward Huizhong. Furious, they could reach Xianyang Bridge in less than three days.

sentences.zh: 此時西南數千里外，得百維州何所用之！

translations.literal: At that time, several thousand li to the southwest, what use would a hundred Weizhou be!
translations.idiomatic: What good would a hundred Weizhous do us then, thousands of li to the southwest?

sentences.zh: 徒棄誠信，有害無利。

translations.literal: In vain abandoning sincerity and faith—harm without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: We would simply sacrifice good faith for nothing gained.

sentences.zh: 此匹夫所不為，況天子乎！」

translations.literal: This even a common man would not do—how much less the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: A common man would not do this—much less the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 上以為然，詔德裕以其城歸吐蕃，執悉怛謀及所與偕來者悉歸之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deemed it so; he ordered Deyu to return the city to Tibet, and Sinam and all who had come with him were seized and all sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed. He ordered Li Deyu to restore the city to Tibet and surrendered Sinam and all his followers.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃盡誅之於境上，極其慘酷。

translations.literal: Tibet executed them all at the border, to the utmost cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans executed every one of them at the frontier with extreme brutality.

sentences.zh: 德裕由是怨僧孺益深。

translations.literal: Deyu for this reason resented Sengru all the more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: From this Li Deyu's resentment of Niu Sengru grew deeper still.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，李德裕奏南詔寇巂州，陷三縣。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuyin: Li Deyu memorialized that Nanzhao raided Xizhou and captured three counties.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, Li Deyu reported that Nanzhao had invaded Xizhou and overrun three counties.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬子，詔以水旱降系囚。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day renzi: an edict was issued to reduce sentences of prisoners held on account of flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renzi, an edict commuted sentences of prisoners in response to floods and drought.

sentences.zh: 群臣上尊號曰太和文武至德皇帝。

translations.literal: The ministers submitted an honorific title: Emperor Taihe Wenwu Zhide.
translations.idiomatic: The court offered the honorific title "Emperor of Grand Harmony, Civil and Military, Supreme Virtue."

sentences.zh: 右補闕韋溫上疏，以為：「今水旱為災，恐非崇飾徽稱之時。」

translations.literal: Right Reminder Wei Wen submitted a memorial, holding that: "Now flood and drought bring disaster—this is scarcely the time to exalt ornamental epithets."
translations.idiomatic: Right Reminder Wei Wen submitted a memorial, arguing: "With flood and drought bringing disaster, this is scarcely the time to exalt ornamental epithets."

sentences.zh: 上善之，辭不受。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved this and declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted the advice and declined the title.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛丑，以武寧節度使王智興兼侍中，充忠武節度使；

translations.literal: Third month, day xinchou: Military Commissioner Wang Zhixing of Wuning was also made Palace Attendant and appointed Military Commissioner of Zhongwu;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinchou, Wang Zhixing, military commissioner of Wuning, was also made Palace Attendant and appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 以邠寧節度使李聽為武寧節度使。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Li Ting of Binning was made Military Commissioner of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting, military commissioner of Binning, was transferred to Wuning.

sentences.zh: 回鶻昭禮可汗為其下所殺，從子胡特勒立。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Zhaoli Qaghan was killed by his subordinates; his nephew Hutele succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur qaghan Zhaoli was murdered by his followers; his nephew Hutele took the throne.

sentences.zh: 李聽之前鎮武寧也，有蒼頭為牙將。

translations.literal: When Li Ting had previously garrisoned Wuning, there was a manservant who served as a guard general.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ting had previously served at Wuning, a household slave held the rank of guard general.

sentences.zh: 至是，聽先遣親吏至徐州慰勞將士，蒼頭不欲聽復來，說軍士殺其親吏，臠食之。

translations.literal: At this time, Ting first sent a personal clerk to Xuzhou to comfort the soldiers; the manservant did not wish Ting to return and persuaded the troops to kill the personal clerk and carve up his flesh to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as Li Ting prepared to return, he sent a personal aide ahead to Xuzhou to greet the garrison. The slave did not want Li Ting back. He incited the soldiers to kill the aide and eat his flesh.

sentences.zh: 聽懼，以疾固辭。

translations.literal: Ting was afraid and firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting, terrified, pleaded illness and refused the post.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以前忠武節度使高瑀為武陵節度使。

translations.literal: On xinyou, former Military Commissioner Gao Yu of Zhongwu was made Military Commissioner of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Gao Yu, former military commissioner of Zhongwu, was appointed military commissioner of Wuning in Li Ting's stead.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，甲辰，李德裕奏修邛崍關及移巂州理台登城。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day jiachen: Li Deyu memorialized on repairing Qionglai Pass and relocating Xizhou's administrative seat to Tai'deng city.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on jiachen, Li Deyu reported repairs to Qionglai Pass and the relocation of Xizhou's seat to Tai'deng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，原王逵薨。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the Prince of Yuan, Kui, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Prince Kui of Yuan died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，立魯王永為太子。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiazi: Prince Yong of Lu was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, Prince Yong of Lu was named Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 初，上以晉王普，敬宗長子，性謹願，欲以為嗣。

translations.literal: Initially the Emperor, because Prince Jin Pu, Emperor Jingzong's eldest son, was by nature prudent and honest, wished to make him heir.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Emperor had intended to name Prince Pu of Jin—Emperor Jingzong's eldest son, a careful and modest man—as his successor.

sentences.zh: 會薨，上痛惜之，故久不議建儲，至是始行之。

translations.literal: He happened to die; the Emperor grieved and mourned him, and therefore for long did not discuss establishing an heir—until now he first carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Pu died, the Emperor mourned deeply and long delayed naming an heir. Only now did he act.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙卯，以荊南節度使段文昌為西川節度使。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day yimao: Military Commissioner Duan Wenchang of Jingnan was made Military Commissioner of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yimao, Duan Wenchang, military commissioner of Jingnan, was transferred to Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 西川監軍王踐言入知樞密，數為上言：「縛送悉怛謀以快虜心，絕後來降者，非計也。」

translations.literal: Xichuan Army Supervisor Wang Jianyan entered service as Director of Palace Secretariat Affairs and repeatedly told the Emperor: "To bind and send Sinam to please the barbarians' hearts cuts off those who would surrender hereafter—not a sound plan."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianyan, Xichuan's army supervisor, entered the privy council and repeatedly warned the Emperor: "Handing Sinam over to please the Tibetans will discourage all future defectors. That was no strategy."

sentences.zh: 上亦悔之，尤中書侍郎、同平章事牛僧孺失策。

translations.literal: The Emperor also regretted it, blaming especially Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Grand Councillor Niu Sengru for the mistaken policy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came to regret the decision and blamed Niu Sengru, Vice Director and Grand Councillor, above all.

sentences.zh: 附李德裕者因言「僧孺與德裕有隙，害其功。」

translations.literal: Those aligned with Li Deyu thereupon said: "Sengru had a rift with Deyu and harmed his achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu's allies added that "Niu Sengru was feuding with Li Deyu and had sabotaged his achievement."

sentences.zh: 上益疏之。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew all the more distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's trust in Niu Sengru waned further.

sentences.zh: 僧孺內不自安，會上御延英，謂宰相曰：「天下何時當太平，卿等亦有意於此乎！」

translations.literal: Sengru inwardly was not at ease; when the Emperor attended Yanying, he said to the chancellors: "When will the realm attain great peace? Do you gentlemen also harbor intentions toward this!"
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Niu Sengru was summoned when the Emperor held court at the Yanying Hall and asked the chancellors, "When will the realm know true peace? Do any of you even aspire to that?"

sentences.zh: 僧孺對曰：「太平無象。

translations.literal: Sengru replied: "Great peace has no fixed form.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru answered, "Great peace has no visible sign.

sentences.zh: 今四夷不至交侵，百姓不至流散，雖非至理，亦謂小康。

translations.literal: Now the four barbarians do not mutually invade, the common people do not flee and scatter—though not the ultimate order, it may be called modest prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier is quiet and the people are not fleeing. That may not be the golden age, but it is peace of a kind.

sentences.zh: 陛下若別求太平，非臣等所及。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty separately seeks great peace, that lies beyond your servants' reach."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty seeks something beyond that, it is more than we can deliver."

sentences.zh: 退，謂同列曰：「主上責望如此，吾曹豈得久居此地乎！」

translations.literal: Withdrawing, he said to his colleagues: "The sovereign's expectations and reproaches being thus, how can we long remain in this place!"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he told his colleagues, "With expectations like that, how long can we remain in office?"

sentences.zh: 因累表請罷。

translations.literal: He thereupon repeatedly submitted memorials requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted repeated requests to resign.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙丑，以僧孺同平章事，充淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day yichou: Sengru was made Co-Equal Grand Councillor and appointed Military Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yichou, Niu Sengru was retained as Grand Councillor while appointed military commissioner of Huainan—effectively removed from court.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：君明臣忠，上令下從，俊良在位，佞邪黜遠，禮修樂舉，刑清政平，奸宄消伏，兵革偃戢，諸侯順附，四夷懷服，時和年豐，家給人足，此太平之象也。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: The ruler enlightened and ministers loyal, commands above and compliance below, the worthy and good in office, flatterers and the wicked dismissed afar, rites cultivated and music raised, punishments clear and government balanced, villains subdued and stilled, arms and armor laid down, feudal lords obediently attached, four barbarians cherishing submission, seasons harmonious and years abundant, households provided and people sufficient—these are the signs of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: When the ruler is wise and ministers loyal, orders run smoothly from above to below; the worthy serve and the wicked are banished; ritual and music flourish, justice is clear and governance sound; crime subsides and war ceases; lords submit and barbarians are tamed; seasons are mild, harvests rich, and every household has enough—these are the marks of true peace.

sentences.zh: 於斯之時，閽寺專權，脅君於內，弗能遠也；

translations.literal: In such a time, gate-and-palace eunuchs monopolize power, coercing the ruler within—he cannot send them afar;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in such an age, eunuchs monopolized power, holding the Emperor hostage within the palace, and he could not banish them;

sentences.zh: 籓鎮阻兵，陵慢於外，弗能制也；

translations.literal: The frontier garrisons blockade with troops, insolent and overbearing without—he cannot control them;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanderies kept armies in the field, defiant and arrogant toward the throne, and he could not restrain them;

sentences.zh: 士卒殺逐主帥，拒命自立，弗能詰也；

translations.literal: Soldiers kill and drive out commanders, defy orders and install themselves—he cannot hold them accountable;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers murdered and expelled their generals, defied imperial orders and installed their own leaders, and he could not punish them;

sentences.zh: 軍旅歲興，賦斂日急，骨血縱橫於原野，杼軸空竭於里閭，而僧孺謂之太平，不亦誣乎！

translations.literal: Armies and campaigns arise year after year, levies and exactions grow daily urgent; flesh and blood lie scattered across the wilds, looms and axles stand emptied in village lanes—yet Sengru calls this great peace—is it not deception!
translations.idiomatic: Campaign followed campaign, taxes grew ever harsher, the dead littered the countryside, and every village was stripped bare—yet Niu Sengru called this peace. What fraud!

sentences.zh: 當文宗求治之時，僧孺任居承弼，進則偷安取容以竊位，退則欺君誣世以盜名，罪孰大焉！

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong sought good governance, Sengru held the office of Chancellor; in advancement he clung to ease and curried favor to steal position, in retreat he deceived the ruler and deceived the age to steal renown—what crime is greater!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong was struggling to restore good governance, Niu Sengru sat as Chancellor—timid and complacent in office, sycophantic to keep his seat, deceiving the Emperor and the realm to preserve his reputation. What offense could be greater?

sentences.zh: 珍王誠薨。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhen, Cheng, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Zhen died.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，昭義節度使劉從諫入朝。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Military Commissioner Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Liu Congjian, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, came to court.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以前西川節度使李德裕為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, the former Military Commissioner of Xichuan, Li Deyu, was made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Li Deyu, former military commissioner of Xichuan, was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 初，李宗閔與德裕有隙，及德裕還自西川，上注意甚厚，朝夕且為相，宗閔百方沮之不能。

translations.literal: At first, Li Zongmin and Deyu had a rift; when Deyu returned from Xichuan, the Emperor's attention to him was very deep, and morning and evening he was nearly to be made Chancellor—Zongmin by every means obstructed this and could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin and Li Deyu had long been rivals. When Deyu returned from Sichuan, the Emperor favored him heavily and was close to naming him Chancellor. Zongmin tried every means to block the appointment but failed.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹杜悰，宗閔黨也，嘗詣宗閔，見其有憂色，曰：「得非以大戎乎？」

translations.literal: Du Cong, Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, was of Zongmin's faction; he once called on Zongmin, saw him with a troubled expression, and said: "Could it not be because of the Great Barbarian?"
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong, Prefect of the Capital and a follower of Li Zongmin, once visited Zongmin and noticed his worried look. "Is it because of the Great Barbarian?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 宗閔曰：「然。

translations.literal: Zongmin said: "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin said, "It is.

sentences.zh: 何以相救？」

translations.literal: How shall we rescue each other?"
translations.idiomatic: How can you help?"

sentences.zh: 悰曰：「悰有一策，可平宿憾，恐公不能用。」

translations.literal: Cong said: "Cong has one stratagem that can settle old resentments—but I fear you, sir, cannot use it."
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong said, "I have a plan that could settle old scores, but I doubt you will accept it."

sentences.zh: 宗閔曰：「何如？」

translations.literal: Zongmin said: "What is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin asked, "What is it?"

sentences.zh: 悰曰：「德裕有文學而不由科第，常用此為慊慊，若使之知舉，必喜矣。」

translations.literal: Cong said: "Deyu has literary talent yet did not enter by the examination route; he often broods on this as a grievance—if he were made chief examiner, he would surely be pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong said, "Deyu is learned but never passed the examinations—a sore point for him. Make him chief examiner of the civil service exams and he will be delighted."

sentences.zh: 宗閔默然有間，曰：「更思其次。」

translations.literal: Zongmin was silent for a space, then said: "Think of the next best."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin was silent a moment, then said, "Think of something else."

sentences.zh: 悰曰：「不則用為御史大夫。」

translations.literal: Cong said: "If not, then appoint him Censor-in-Chief."
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong said, "Then appoint him Censor-in-Chief."

sentences.zh: 宗閔曰：「此則可矣。」

translations.literal: Zongmin said: "That will do."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin said, "That will do."

sentences.zh: 悰再三與約，乃詣德裕。

translations.literal: Cong repeatedly sealed the agreement with him, then went to call on Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: After confirming the plan several times, Du Cong went to see Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 德裕迎揖曰：「公何為訪此寂寥？」

translations.literal: Deyu came forward with a bow and said: "Why does the Duke visit this deserted place?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu greeted him with a bow: "Why visit someone so forsaken as I?"

sentences.zh: 悰曰：「靖安相公令悰達意。」

translations.literal: Cong said: "The Duke of Jing'an ordered Cong to convey his intent."
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong said, "The Duke of Jing'an sent me to deliver a message."

sentences.zh: 即以大夫之命告之。

translations.literal: He thereupon told him of the Censor-in-Chief appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He told Li Deyu of the Censor-in-Chief appointment.

sentences.zh: 德裕驚喜泣下，曰：「此大門官，小子何足以當之！」

translations.literal: Deyu, in surprise and joy, wept and said: "This is the grand gate office—how can this little man be worthy of it!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu wept with surprise and joy: "That is the great censorate—I am hardly worthy!"

sentences.zh: 寄謝重沓。

translations.literal: He sent repeated thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He sent message after message of thanks.

sentences.zh: 宗閔復與給事中楊虞卿謀之，事遂中止。

translations.literal: Zongmin again plotted the matter with Palace Drafting Attendant Yang Yuqing, and the affair thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin then consulted Palace Drafting Attendant Yang Yuqing, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 虞卿，汝士之從弟也。

translations.literal: Yuqing was the younger cousin of Rushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuqing was a younger cousin of Yang Rushi.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲午，加昭義節度使劉從諫同平章事，遣歸鎮。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day jiawu: Military Commissioner Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi was given the additional title Co-Equal Grand Councillor and sent back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiawu, Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi was made an honorary Grand Councillor and sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 初，從諫以忠義自任，入朝，欲請他鎮。

translations.literal: At first, Congjian took righteousness and loyalty upon himself; entering court, he wished to request another command.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian had styled himself a man of loyalty. When he came to court, he meant to ask for transfer to another post.

sentences.zh: 既至，見朝廷事柄不一，又士大夫多請托，心輕朝廷，故歸而益驕。

translations.literal: Once arrived, seeing that court authority was not unified and that many scholar-officials sought patronage, he looked down on the court in his heart; therefore on returning he grew all the more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he saw a divided court and officials trading favors everywhere. He lost respect for the capital and returned to his province more arrogant than before.

sentences.zh: 徐州承王智興之後，士卒驕悖，節度使高瑀不能制，上以為憂。

translations.literal: Xuzhou, inheriting after Wang Zhixing, had soldiers insolent and rebellious; Military Commissioner Gao Yu could not control them—the Emperor regarded this with concern.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou had been unruly since Wang Zhixing's day. The troops were insubordinate and Military Commissioner Gao Yu could not control them. The Emperor was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以嶺南節度使崔珙為武寧節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Military Commissioner Cui Gong of Lingnan was made Military Commissioner of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Cui Gong, military commissioner of Lingnan, was transferred to Wuning.

sentences.zh: 珙至鎮，寬猛適宜，徐人安之。

translations.literal: Gong arrived at his command; lenience and severity were appropriately balanced, and the people of Xu were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong governed with a balance of firmness and mercy, and the region settled down.

sentences.zh: 珙，琯之弟也。

translations.literal: Gong was the younger brother of Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong was the younger brother of Cui Guan.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸亥，加盧龍節度使、檢校工部尚書楊志誠檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Second month, day guihai: Military Commissioner of Lulong, Supervisory Minister of Works Yang Zhicheng, was given the additional supervisory title Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guihai, Yang Zhicheng, military commissioner of Lulong and honorary Minister of Works, was promoted to honorary Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 進奏官徐迪詣宰相言：「軍中不識朝廷之制，唯知尚書改僕射為遷，不知工部改吏部為美，敕使往，恐不得出。」

translations.literal: Memorial presentation officer Xu Di called on the chancellors and said: "The army does not understand court regulations—it only knows that changing from Minister to Vice Minister is promotion, and does not know that changing from Works to Personnel is an honor; if an edict envoy goes, I fear he will not be allowed to leave."
translations.idiomatic: Memorial officer Xu Di told the chancellors: "The troops know nothing of court rank. They think a change from Minister to Vice Minister is a promotion—they do not see Works to Personnel as an honor. Send an imperial envoy and he may never leave alive."

sentences.zh: 辭氣甚慢，宰相不以為意。

translations.literal: His tone was very insolent; the chancellors did not take it seriously.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with brazen insolence. The chancellors paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以兵部尚書李德裕同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Minister of War Li Deyu was made Co-Equal Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Li Deyu, Minister of War, was appointed Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 德裕入謝，上與之論朋黨事，對曰：「方今朝士三分之一為朋黨。」

translations.literal: Deyu entered to give thanks; the Emperor discussed factional matters with him. He answered: "At present a third of court scholars are in factions."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu came to give thanks, the Emperor raised the problem of cliques. Li Deyu replied, "At present a third of court officials belong to factions."

sentences.zh: 時給事中楊虞卿與從兄中書舍人汝士、弟戶部郎中漢公、中書舍人張元夫、給事中蕭澣等善交結，依附權要，上干執政，下撓有司，為士人求官及科第，無不如志，上聞而惡之，故與德裕言首及之。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Drafting Attendant Yang Yuqing, with his elder cousin Secretariat Drafting Officer Rushi, his younger brother Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Hangong, Secretariat Drafting Officer Zhang Yuanfu, and Palace Drafting Attendant Xiao Huan, formed close associations, clinging to the powerful; above they importuned the chancellors, below they obstructed officials, seeking offices and examination success for scholars—all without fail as they wished. The Emperor heard and hated this; therefore in speaking with Deyu he mentioned it first.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuqing had cultivated a network with his cousin Yang Rushi, a secretariat drafting officer; his brother Hangong, vice director in the Ministry of Revenue; Zhang Yuanfu, also a secretariat drafting officer; and Xiao Huan, a palace drafting attendant. They traded on connections to the powerful, pressured the chancellors from above and officials below, and secured appointments and examination passes for their clients—always successfully. The Emperor hated this and raised the subject first with Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 德裕因得以排其所不悅者。

translations.literal: Deyu thereupon was able to purge those he disliked.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu seized the opportunity to purge his enemies.

sentences.zh: 初，左散騎常侍張仲方嘗駁李吉甫謚，及德裕為相，仲方稱疾不出。

translations.literal: At first, Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Zhongfang had once opposed Li Jiyu's posthumous title; when Deyu became Chancellor, Zhongfang claimed illness and did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: Left Cavalier Attendant Zhang Zhongfang had once challenged Li Jiyu's posthumous title. When Li Deyu became Chancellor, Zhongfang pleaded illness and stayed away from court.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬辰，以仲方為賓客分司。

translations.literal: Third month, day renchen: Zhongfang was made Honorary Retainer in detached service.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renchen, Zhang Zhongfang was sidelined as honorary retainer in detached service.

sentences.zh: 楊志誠怒不得僕射，留官告使魏寶義並春衣使焦奉鸞、送奚、契丹使尹士恭。

translations.literal: Yang Zhicheng, enraged at not receiving the Vice Ministry, detained credential envoy Wei Baoyi together with spring-garment envoy Jiao Fengluan and the envoy escorting Xi and Khitan, Yin Shigong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhicheng, furious at not receiving the Vice Ministry, detained credential envoy Wei Baoyi, spring-garment envoy Jiao Fengluan, and Yin Shigong, envoy to the Xi and Khitan.

sentences.zh: 甲午，遣牙將王文穎來謝恩並讓官。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, he dispatched military adjutant Wang Wenying to express thanks for imperial favor and decline the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he sent adjutant Wang Wenying to thank the court—and refuse the promotion.

sentences.zh: 丙申，復以告身並批答賜之，文穎不受而去。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, the court again granted credential and written reply; Wenying would not accept and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the court sent the appointment again with an imperial reply. Wang Wenying refused it and left.

sentences.zh: 和王綺薨。

translations.literal: The Prince of He, Qi, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi of He died.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以楊虞卿為常州刺史，張元夫為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Yang Yuqing was made Prefect of Changzhou, and Zhang Yuanfu Prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Yang Yuqing was demoted to prefect of Changzhou and Zhang Yuanfu to prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 它日，上復言及朋黨，李宗閔曰：「臣素知之，故虞卿輩臣皆不與美官。」

translations.literal: Another day, the Emperor again spoke of factions; Li Zongmin said: "Your servant has long known this; therefore I have never given Yuqing and his group fine offices."
translations.idiomatic: On another day the Emperor spoke of factions again. Li Zongmin said, "I have known about them for years—that is why I never gave Yuqing and his circle desirable posts."

sentences.zh: 李德裕曰：「給、捨非美官而何！」

translations.literal: Li Deyu said: "Palace drafting and secretariat posts—if not fine offices, then what are they!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu shot back, "Palace drafting and secretariat posts—what finer offices are there?"

sentences.zh: 宗閔失色。

translations.literal: Zongmin lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin went pale.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以蕭浣為鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, Xiao Huan was made Prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Xiao Huan was appointed prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙戌，冊回鶻新可汗為愛登裡囉汩沒密施合句祿毘伽彰信可汗。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingxu: the new Khagan of the Uyghurs was enfeoffed as Idimlyan Qutlugh Bilge Khan Aixin Zhangxin.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingxu, the new Uyghur khagan was invested as Idimlyan Qutlugh Bilge Khan Aixin Zhangxin.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙巳，以山南西道節度使李載義為河東節度使。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day yisi: Military Commissioner Li Zaiyi of Shannan West Circuit was made Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yisi, Li Zaiyi, military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, was transferred to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 先是，回鶻每入貢，所過暴掠，州縣不敢詰，但嚴兵防衛而已。

translations.literal: Before this, whenever the Uyghurs came to pay tribute, they plundered violently along the route; prefectures and counties dared not investigate, but only tightened troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, whenever Uyghur tribute missions passed through, they looted freely. Local officials dared not intervene and could only post guards.

sentences.zh: 載義至鎮，回鶻使者李暢入貢，載義謂之曰：「可汗遣將軍入貢，以固舅甥之好，非遣將軍陵踐上國也。

translations.literal: Zaiyi arrived at his command; Uyghur envoy Li Chang came to pay tribute. Zaiyi said to him: "The Khagan dispatched the general to pay tribute in order to solidify the uncle-nephew friendship—not to send the general to trample the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zaiyi took up his post, the Uyghur envoy Li Chang arrived on tribute business. Li Zaiyi told him, "Your khagan sent you to strengthen the bond of kinship between our courts—not to let you run roughshod over the empire.

sentences.zh: 將軍不戢部曲，使為侵盜。

translations.literal: The general does not restrain his troops, causing them to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot control your men and they keep pillaging—

sentences.zh: 載義亦得殺之，勿謂中國之法可忽也。」

translations.literal: Zaiyi likewise may kill them—do not suppose the laws of the Middle Kingdom may be disregarded."
translations.idiomatic: I am entitled to execute them. Do not imagine that Chinese law counts for nothing."

sentences.zh: 於是悉罷防衛兵，但使二卒守其門。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entirely dismissed the guard troops, assigning only two soldiers to watch his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed all guard detachments and posted only two soldiers at Li Chang's gate.

sentences.zh: 暢畏服，不敢犯令。

translations.literal: Chang feared and submitted, and dared not violate the order.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chang was cowed and did not dare disobey.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以工部尚書鄭覃為御史大夫。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Minister of Works Zheng Tan was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Zheng Tan, Minister of Works, was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 初，李宗閔惡覃在禁中數言事，奏罷其侍講。

translations.literal: At first, Li Zongmin hated that Tan in the inner palace frequently spoke on affairs; he memorialized to remove him from the lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin had resented Zheng Tan's frequent counsel in the inner palace and had him removed from his post as imperial lecturer.

sentences.zh: 上從容謂宰相曰：「殷侑經術頗似鄭覃。」

translations.literal: The Emperor casually said to the chancellors: "Yin You's classical learning is rather like Zheng Tan's."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor remarked casually to the chancellors, "Yin You's scholarship reminds me of Zheng Tan's."

sentences.zh: 宗閔對曰：「覃、侑經術誠可尚，然論議不足聽。」

translations.literal: Zongmin answered: "Tan and You's classical learning is indeed admirable, yet their policy discussions are not worth hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin replied, "Their learning is admirable, but their political counsel is not worth hearing."

sentences.zh: 李德裕曰：「覃、侑議論，他人不欲聞，惟陛下欲聞之。」

translations.literal: Li Deyu said: "Tan and You's policy discussions—others do not wish to hear them; only Your Majesty wishes to hear them."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, "Others may not want to hear Zheng Tan and Yin You—but Your Majesty does."

sentences.zh: 後旬日，宣出，除覃御史大夫。

translations.literal: Ten-odd days later, an edict was issued from the palace: Tan was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later an imperial edict bypassing the chancellors appointed Zheng Tan Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 宗閔謂樞密使崔潭峻曰：「事一切宣出，安用中書！」

translations.literal: Zongmin said to Chief Palace Secretariat Commissioner Cui Tanjun: "When all affairs are issued from the palace proclamation, what use is the Secretariat!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin told Chief Palace Secretariat Commissioner Cui Tanjun, "If everything is issued straight from the palace, what need is there for the Secretariat?"

sentences.zh: 譚峻曰：「八年天子，聽其自行事亦可矣！」

translations.literal: Tanjun said: "An emperor of eight years—let him conduct his own affairs, and that may suffice!"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tanjun replied, "He has been Emperor for eight years—let him do as he chooses!"

sentences.zh: 宗閔愀然而止。

translations.literal: Zongmin, with a changed expression, ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin fell silent, his face grim.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以中書侍郎、同平章事李宗閔同平章事、充山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Grand Councillor Li Zongmin was retained as Co-Equal Grand Councillor and appointed Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Li Zongmin was retained as Grand Councillor while being sent out as military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit—effectively removed from court.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬寅，以右僕射王涯同平章事、兼度支、鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day renyin: Right Vice Minister Wang Ya was made Co-Equal Grand Councillor and concurrently Commissioner of Revenue, Salt, and Iron Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, Wang Ya, Right Vice Minister, was made Grand Councillor and commissioner of revenue, salt, and iron transport.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使楊元卿有疾，朝廷議除代，李德裕請徙劉從諫於宣武，因拔出上黨，不使與山東連結。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Yang Yuanqing of Xuanwu was ill; the court discussed replacement. Li Deyu requested transferring Liu Congjian to Xuanwu, thereby pulling him out of Shangdang and preventing linkage with the Shandong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Yang Yuanqing of Xuanwu fell ill. The court debated his replacement. Li Deyu proposed moving Liu Congjian to Xuanwu—extracting him from Shangdang before he could ally with the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 上以為未可。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered it not yet feasible.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought the plan premature.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以左僕射李程為宣武節度使。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Left Vice Minister Li Cheng was made Military Commissioner of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Li Cheng, Left Vice Minister, was appointed military commissioner of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 上患近世文士不通經術，李德裕請依楊綰議，進士試論議，不試詩賦。

translations.literal: The Emperor grieved that recent literati did not comprehend classical learning; Li Deyu requested following Yang Guan's proposal—that jinshi candidates be examined on policy essays, not poetry and rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor lamented that modern literati lacked classical learning. Li Deyu proposed following Yang Guan's plan: jinshi candidates would be tested on policy essays, not poetry and fu.

sentences.zh: 德裕又言：「昔玄宗以臨淄王定內難，自是疑忌宗室，不令出閣。

translations.literal: Deyu also said: "Formerly Emperor Xuanzong, as Prince of Linzi, settled an internal crisis; from then on he was suspicious of the imperial clan and did not allow them to leave the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu added, "When Emperor Xuanzong was still Prince of Linzi, he crushed a rebellion within the palace. Ever after he distrusted the imperial clan and kept princes confined to the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 天下議皆以為幽閉骨肉，虧傷人倫。

translations.literal: Public opinion throughout the realm held that secluding one's kin wounded human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that cloistering one's own blood kin violated the bonds of family.

sentences.zh: 向使天寶之末、建中這初，宗室散處方州，雖未能安定王室，尚可各全其生。

translations.literal: Had the imperial clan been dispersed to the provinces at the end of the Tianbao era and the beginning of the Jianzhong era, though they might not have stabilized the royal house, each could still have preserved his life.
translations.idiomatic: Had princes been dispersed to the provinces before the Tianbao and Jianzhong crises, they might not have saved the dynasty, but each could at least have saved his own life.

sentences.zh: 所以悉為安祿山、朱泚所魚肉者，由聚於一宮故也。

translations.literal: The reason all were cut up like fish and meat by An Lushan and Zhu Ci was that they were gathered in one palace.
translations.idiomatic: The reason An Lushan and Zhu Ci were able to slaughter them all was that they had been packed into a single palace compound.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠因冊太子，制書聽宗室年高屬疏者出閣，且除諸州上佐，使攜其男女出外婚嫁。

translations.literal: Your Majesty truly should, upon investing the Crown Prince, issue a decree allowing clansmen who are advanced in years or distant in lineage to leave the inner quarters, and appoint them senior aides in the various prefectures, enabling them to take their sons and daughters outside to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should use the investiture of the Crown Prince to decree that elder and more distant princes may leave the inner quarters, appoint them senior adjutants in the provinces, and let them marry off their sons and daughters outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 此則百年弊法，一旦因陛下去之，海內孰不欣悅！」

translations.literal: This would be a hundred-year-old abusive practice—abolished at once by Your Majesty; who throughout the realm would not rejoice!"
translations.idiomatic: A hundred-year-old abuse, swept away in a single stroke—who in the empire would not rejoice?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「茲事朕久知其不可，方今諸王豈無賢才，無所施耳！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "On this matter I have long known it cannot be done; as for the princes today, are there none among them with talent? They simply have nowhere to apply it!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I have known for years that this cannot be done—and today's princes are not without talent. They simply have no scope to prove it!"

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，冊命太子，因下制：諸王自今以次出閣，授緊、望州刺史、上佐；

translations.literal: Eighth month, day gengyin: the Crown Prince was invested; thereupon a decree was issued: princes from now on shall leave the inner quarters in succession, receiving appointment as prefects or senior aides of close and prestigious prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengyin, the Crown Prince was invested. A decree followed: princes would leave the inner quarters in order and receive appointments as prefects or senior adjutants of important prefectures;

sentences.zh: 十六宅縣主，以時出適；

translations.literal: county princesses of the Sixteen Residences shall marry out in due season;
translations.idiomatic: county princesses of the Sixteen Residences would marry at the proper time;

sentences.zh: 進士停試詩賦。

translations.literal: jinshi candidates cease examination in poetry and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: and jinshi examinations would drop poetry and fu.

sentences.zh: 諸王出閣，竟以議所除官不決而罷。

translations.literal: The princes' leaving the inner quarters ultimately was abandoned because discussion of the offices to be assigned could not be decided.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the plan to release the princes came to nothing—the court could not agree on what posts to assign them.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，加幽州節度使楊志誠檢校右僕射，仍別遣使慰諭之。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Military Commissioner Yang Zhicheng of Youzhou was given the additional supervisory title Right Vice Minister, and a separate envoy was dispatched to console and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Yang Zhicheng of Youzhou was given the honorary title Right Vice Minister, and a separate envoy was sent to placate him.

sentences.zh: 杜牧憤河朔三鎮之桀驁，而朝廷議者專事姑息，乃作書，名曰《罪言》，大略以為：「國家自天寶盜起，河北百餘城不得尺寸，人望之若回鶻、吐蕃，無敢窺者。

translations.literal: Du Mu, indignant at the insolence of the three Hebei circuits, while court debaters devoted themselves solely to indulgence, wrote a work entitled "Accusatory Discourse," roughly holding: "Since the rebellion arose in the Tianbao era, not an inch of the hundred-odd cities of Hebei has been recovered; men look upon them as upon the Uyghurs and Tibetans—none dares to gaze upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Du Mu, enraged by the arrogance of the three Hebei circuits and by a court policy of endless indulgence, wrote a work called Accusatory Discourse. Its gist: "Since the Tianbao rebellion, not one of Hebei's hundred-odd cities had been recovered. Men looked upon them as they did the Uyghurs and Tibetans—too dangerous even to watch.

sentences.zh: 齊、梁、蔡被其風流，因亦為寇。

translations.literal: Qi, Liang, and Cai caught their drift and likewise became marauders.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, Liang, and Cai caught the contagion and turned to rebellion themselves.

sentences.zh: 未嘗五年間不戰，焦焦然七十餘年矣。

translations.literal: There has scarcely been a five-year span without warfare—burning hot for more than seventy years.
translations.idiomatic: There had scarcely been five peaceful years in a row. The country had been at war, seething, for more than seventy years.

sentences.zh: 今上策莫如先自治，中策莫如取魏，最下策為浪戰，不計地勢，不審攻守是也。」

translations.literal: Now the superior strategy is none better than first governing oneself; the middle strategy none better than taking Wei; the lowest strategy is reckless warfare—not calculating terrain, not examining attack and defense—is precisely this."
translations.idiomatic: The best policy was to put the empire in order first. The second best was to seize Wei. The worst was blind warfare—fighting without regard to terrain or the balance of offense and defense."

sentences.zh: 又傷府兵廢壞，作《原十六衛》，以為：「國家始踵隋制，開十六衛，自今觀之，設官言無謂者，其十六衛乎！

translations.literal: Grieved also at the decay of the frontier garrison system, he wrote "On the Sixteen Guards," holding: "The state at first followed Sui institutions and established the Sixteen Guards—viewed from today, of offices established that speak of nothing meaningful, are they not the Sixteen Guards!
translations.idiomatic: Grieved also by the decay of the garrison militia, he wrote On the Sixteen Guards, arguing: "The state had followed Sui practice in establishing the Sixteen Guards—but viewed from the present, what office could be more pointless?

sentences.zh: 本原事跡，其實天下之大命也。

translations.literal: In their original trace and root affairs, they are in truth the great mandate of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In origin and function, they had been nothing less than the fate of the empire.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，內以十六衛蓄養武臣，外開折衝、果毅府五百七十四，以儲兵伍；

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, within, the Sixteen Guards nurtured military officers; without, five hundred seventy-four assault-and-boldness commanderies were opened to store troops;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong, the Sixteen Guards within the capital nurtured military officers, while five hundred seventy-four frontier garrison commands stored troops without;

sentences.zh: 有事則戎臣提兵居外，無事則放兵居內。

translations.literal: when there was business, military officers led troops and dwelt outside; when there was none, troops were released to dwell within.
translations.idiomatic: in crisis, officers led their men in the field; in peace, those troops returned to garrison duty inside the capital.

sentences.zh: 其居內也，富貴恩澤以奉養其身，所部之兵散捨諸府。

translations.literal: When dwelling within, wealth, honor, and imperial grace nourished their persons; the troops under their command were dispersed among the various commands.
translations.idiomatic: While garrisoned within, officers lived on imperial favor while their troops were dispersed among the garrison commands.

sentences.zh: 上府不越千二百人，三時耕稼，一時治武，籍藏將府，伍散田畝，力解勢破，人人自愛，雖有蚩尤為帥，亦不可使為亂耳。

translations.literal: Upper commands did not exceed twelve hundred men; three seasons farming, one season training in arms; rolls stored in the general's command, companies scattered in fields—strength dissolved, momentum broken, each man cherishing himself; though Chiyou were commander, he still could not be made to raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: No command exceeded twelve hundred men. Three seasons they farmed; one season they drilled. Rolls were kept at headquarters while companies were scattered across the fields—strength divided, cohesion broken, every man looking to his own interests. Even with Chiyou as commander, rebellion would have been impossible.

sentences.zh: 及其居外也，緣部之兵被檄乃來，斧鉞在前，爵賞在後，飄暴交捽，豈暇異略！

translations.literal: When they dwelt outside, troops of the border commands came only when summoned by decree; axes and halberds before, titles and rewards behind—swift storm and violent clash; how could there be leisure for divergent schemes!
translations.idiomatic: When deployed outside, border troops answered only to summons. Executioners marched at the van, rewards followed behind—men hurled together in battle. Who had time for plotting?

sentences.zh: 雖有蚩尤為帥，亦無能為叛也。

translations.literal: Though Chiyou were commander, still none could rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Even Chiyou could not have led them to rebel.

sentences.zh: 自貞觀至於開元百三十年間，戎臣兵伍未始逆篡，此大聖人所以能柄統輕重，制鄣表裡，聖算神術也。

translations.literal: From Zhenguan to Kaiyuan, a span of one hundred thirty years, military officers and soldier companies never once rebelled or usurped—this is why the great sage could wield the balance of heavy and light, control inner and outer barriers, by sacred calculation and divine art.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhenguan through Kaiyuan—one hundred thirty years—no military officer or garrison ever mutinied. That was how the great sage held the balance of power between center and frontier: divine strategy.

sentences.zh: 至於開元末，愚儒奏章曰：『天下文勝矣，請罷府兵。』

translations.literal: By the end of Kaiyuan, foolish scholars memorialized: "The realm's culture has prevailed—please abolish the garrison militia."
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Kaiyuan era, foolish scholars memorialized: "Culture has triumphed throughout the empire—abolish the garrison militia."

sentences.zh: 武夫奏章曰：『天下力強矣，請搏四夷。』

translations.literal: Martial men memorialized: "The realm's strength is great—please grapple with the four barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Warriors memorialized: "The empire is strong—let us crush the four barbarians."

sentences.zh: 於是府兵內鏟，邊兵外作，戎臣兵伍，湍奔矢往，內無一人矣。

translations.literal: So the garrison militia was cut away within, border troops deployed without; military officers and soldier companies, rushing like torrents and flying like arrows—within there was not a single man left.
translations.idiomatic: So the garrison militia was dismantled within the capital while border troops were posted without. Officers and soldiers surged outward like rushing water and flying arrows—until within the palace not a single armed man remained.

sentences.zh: 尾大中干，成燕偏重，而天下掀然，根萌燼燃，七聖旰食，求欲除之且不能也。

translations.literal: The tail grew large while the trunk grew dry, becoming like the swallows' heavy imbalance; and the realm was unsettled, roots smoldering into flame—seven sage emperors ate late into the night, seeking to remove it yet unable.
translations.idiomatic: The periphery swelled while the center withered, like a bird grown tail-heavy. The realm trembled; embers at the roots burst into flame. Seven emperors ate late into the night trying to uproot the evil—and could not.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，戎臣兵伍，豈可一日使出落鈴鍵哉！

translations.literal: Viewed from this, military officers and soldier companies—how can they for a single day be allowed to slip their bells and chains!
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows: military officers and their troops must never for a single day be loosed from bell and chain.

sentences.zh: 然為國者不能無兵，居外則叛，居內則篡。

translations.literal: Yet one who governs a state cannot do without troops—stationed without they rebel, stationed within they usurp.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no state can do without soldiers. Post them outside and they rebel; keep them inside and they usurp the throne.

sentences.zh: 使外不叛，內不篡，古今已還，法術最長，其置府立衛乎！

translations.literal: To make those without not rebel and those within not usurp—from antiquity to the present, no method is superior—are they not the establishing of garrison commands and the Sixteen Guards!
translations.idiomatic: To keep outer troops from rebelling and inner troops from seizing power—the finest method since antiquity is surely the garrison command system and the Sixteen Guards!

sentences.zh: 近代已來，於其將也，弊復為甚，率皆市兒輩多繼金玉、負倚幽陰、折券交貨所能致也。

translations.literal: In recent times, regarding their generals, the abuse has again grown extreme—almost all are marketplace youths who inherit gold and jade, lean on hidden patrons, and procure position through trading promissory notes and bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In recent generations the abuse has grown worse still. Most commanders are market-town upstarts who inherit wealth, lean on hidden patrons, and buy their commissions with promissory notes and bribes.

sentences.zh: 絕不識父兄禮義之教，復無慷慨感概之氣。

translations.literal: They utterly know not the instruction of fathers and elder brothers in rites and righteousness, and likewise lack the spirit of magnanimous indignation.
translations.idiomatic: They know nothing of the rites and righteousness taught by fathers and elders, and lack all generous, principled spirit.

sentences.zh: 百城千里，一朝得之，其強傑愎勃者則撓削法制，不使縛己，斬族忠良，不使違己，力壹勢便，罔不為寇。

translations.literal: A hundred cities and a thousand li, obtained in a single morning—the strong, fierce, obstinate, and explosive among them then bend and pare away laws and institutions, not allowing themselves to be bound; they execute clans of the loyal and good, not allowing opposition to themselves; power unified, momentum convenient—all without exception become marauders.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li of territory, a hundred cities—they seize it overnight. The bold and obstinate bend the law to suit themselves, execute loyal families that oppose them, concentrate all power in their hands, and every one becomes a plunderer.

sentences.zh: 其陰泥巧狡者，亦能家算口斂，委於邪幸，由卿市公，去郡得都，四履所治，指為別館。

translations.literal: Those crafty and cunning in secret can also, by household reckoning and mouth by mouth collection, entrust themselves to wicked favorites—from minister they buy their way to duke, from prefecture they reach the capital; wherever their four feet tread in their jurisdiction, they designate private lodges.
translations.idiomatic: The cunning sort amass wealth through household levies, pawn themselves to corrupt favorites, buy advancement from minister to duke, jump from prefect to capital, and mark every district they pass through as their private estate.

sentences.zh: 或一夫不幸而壽，則戛割生人，略幣天下。

translations.literal: If by misfortune one man lives long, then he butchers the living and strips the realm's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Should one such man live out his years, he butchers the living and strips the empire bare.

sentences.zh: 是以天下兵亂不息，齊人乾耗，靡不由是矣。

translations.literal: Therefore warfare and chaos throughout the realm cease not; the people of Qi are drained dry—none of this but flows from this cause.
translations.idiomatic: Hence unending war and the exhaustion of the people—all of it flows from this.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 文皇帝十六衛之旨，其誰原而復之乎！」

translations.literal: The intent of the Sixteen Guards of the Cultural Emperor—who can trace it and restore it!"
translations.idiomatic: Who can recover the intent of Emperor Taizong's Sixteen Guards!"

sentences.zh: 又作《戰論》，以為：「河北視天下，猶珠璣也；

translations.literal: He also wrote "On Warfare," holding: "Hebei views the realm as pearls and jade;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote On Warfare, arguing: "Hebei to the empire is like pearls and jade;

sentences.zh: 天下視河北，猶四支也。

translations.literal: The realm views Hebei as the four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: the empire to Hebei is like limbs to a body.

sentences.zh: 河北氣俗渾厚，果於戰耕，加以土息健馬，便於馳敵，是以出則勝，處則饒，不窺天下之產，自可封殖。

translations.literal: Hebei's air and customs are robust and thick; they excel at fighting and farming; added to this, soil at rest and strong horses make it convenient for charging the enemy—therefore going forth they conquer, dwelling they are rich, not coveting the realm's produce, they can enrich themselves on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei's air and customs are robust; its people excel at fighting and farming. Rich soil and strong horses make them swift against enemies. They conquer when they march forth and prosper when they stay home—without coveting the empire's resources, they can flourish on their own.

sentences.zh: 亦猶大農之家，不待珠璣然後以為富也。

translations.literal: It is also like a great farming household—not needing pearls and jade before considering itself wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Like a great farming family that does not need pearls and jade to count itself rich.

sentences.zh: 國家無河北，則精甲、銳卒、利刀、良弓、健馬無有也，是一支，兵去矣。

translations.literal: If the state lacks Hebei, then fine armor, sharp soldiers, keen blades, good bows, and strong horses are not to be had—this is one limb; the troops are gone.
translations.idiomatic: Without Hebei the state loses fine armor, elite troops, sharp blades, good bows, and strong horses—the first limb, and its army with it.

sentences.zh: 河東、盟津、滑台、大梁、彭城、東平，盡宿厚兵以塞虜沖，不可它使，是二支，兵去矣。

translations.literal: Hedong, Mengjin, Huatai, Daliang, Pengcheng, and Dongping—all garrison heavily to block barbarian thrusts, usable for nothing else—this is the second limb; the troops are gone.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong, Mengjin, Huatai, Daliang, Pengcheng, and Dongping—all garrisoned heavily to block barbarian thrusts and usable for nothing else—the second limb, and its army with it.

sentences.zh: 六鎮之師，厥數三億，低首仰給，橫拱不為，則沿淮已北，循河之南，東盡海，西叩洛，赤地盡取，才能應費，是三支，財去矣。

translations.literal: The armies of the six circuits—their number three hundred thousand—bow their heads receiving rations, arms folded doing nothing; then north of the Huai, south along the Yellow River, east to the sea, west knocking at Luoyang, bare ground entirely taken—only then can expenses be met—this is the third limb; wealth is gone.
translations.idiomatic: The six frontier circuits field three hundred thousand men who bow their heads for imperial rations and do nothing in return. To support them the state must strip everything north of the Huai, south of the Yellow River, east to the sea and west to Luoyang bare—only then can it meet the expense. The third limb, and its wealth with it.

sentences.zh: 咸陽西北，戎夷大屯，盡鏟吳、越、荊、楚之饒以啖兵戍，是四支，財去矣。

translations.literal: Northwest of Xianyang, barbarians mass in great encampments; all the riches of Wu, Yue, Jing, and Chu are scraped to feed the garrison troops—this is the fourth limb; wealth is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Xianyang barbarians mass in force; the riches of Wu, Yue, Jing, and Chu are scraped bare to feed the garrisons—the fourth limb, and its wealth with it.

sentences.zh: 天下四支盡解，頭腹兀然，其能以是久為安乎！

translations.literal: The realm's four limbs all severed, head and belly stand empty—how can it long endure in peace thus!
translations.idiomatic: When all four limbs are severed, head and belly stand empty—how can the body long endure in peace!

sentences.zh: 今者誠能治其五敗，則一戰可定，四支可生。

translations.literal: Now if one can truly remedy the five defeats, then one battle can settle it and the four limbs can live.
translations.idiomatic: If the five causes of defeat can truly be remedied, one battle can settle the issue and the four limbs can be restored.

sentences.zh: 夫天下無事之時，殿寄大臣偷安奉私，戰士離落，兵甲鈍弊，是不蒐練之過，其敗一也。

translations.literal: When the realm is at peace, entrusted ministers grow complacent and self-serving, soldiers drift apart, arms and armor grow dull and worn—this is the fault of not drilling and training; the first defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime entrusted ministers grow complacent and self-serving; soldiers drift apart; arms and armor rust—the first defeat: failure to drill and train.

sentences.zh: 百人荷戈，仰食縣官，則挾千夫之名，大將小裨，操其餘贏，以虜壯為幸，以師老為娛，是執兵者常少，糜食常多，此不責實料食之過，其敗二也。

translations.literal: A hundred men carry halberds, eating from the county offices, yet claim the names of a thousand; great generals and minor aides keep the surplus for themselves, take strong enemies as fortune, take stale campaigns as amusement—those who wield arms are always few, those who waste rations always many—this is the fault of not verifying accounts and rations; the second defeat.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred men carry halberds while eating from the state, yet claim the names of a thousand; generals great and small keep the surplus for themselves, pray for strong enemies and treat a stale campaign as sport—always too few who fight, always too many who eat. The second defeat: failing to verify headcounts and rations.

sentences.zh: 戰小勝則張皇其功，奔走獻狀以邀上賞，或一日再賜，或一月累封，凱還未歌，書品已崇，爵命極矣，田宮廣矣，金繒溢矣，子孫官矣，焉肯搜奇出死，勤於我矣！

translations.literal: After a small victory they inflate their merits, rush about presenting reports to seek imperial reward—sometimes double bounty in a day, sometimes accumulated enfeoffments in a month; before the victory songs are sung, written commissions are already elevated, ranks and titles at their peak, estates and palaces broad, gold and silk overflowing, children and grandchildren given office—how would they seek out danger and risk death, laboring for us!
translations.idiomatic: After a minor victory they inflate their merits, rush memorials to court for rewards—a double bounty in a day, accumulated enfeoffments in a month. Before the victory songs are sung, commissions are raised, ranks maxed out, estates enlarged, gold and silk overflowing, children given office—who would then search out danger and risk death for the state!

sentences.zh: 此厚賞之過，其敗三也。

translations.literal: This is the fault of lavish rewards; the third defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The third defeat: rewards too lavish.

sentences.zh: 多喪兵士，顛翻大都，則跳身而來，刺邦而去。

translations.literal: After many lost soldiers and overturned great capitals, they simply jump to a new post—stab one province and depart.
translations.idiomatic: After heavy losses and the fall of great cities they simply jump to a new post—stabbing one province before deserting to the next.

sentences.zh: 回視刀鋸，氣色甚安，一歲未更，旋已立於壇墀之上矣，此輕罰之過，其敗四也。

translations.literal: They glance back at axe and saw, their expression very calm; within a year, not yet rotated, they already stand upon the review platform—this is the fault of light punishment; the fourth defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They glance back at the executioner's blade unmoved; within a year, not yet rotated, they stand again on the review platform. The fourth defeat: punishments too light.

sentences.zh: 大將兵柄不得專，恩臣、敕使迭來揮之，堂然將陳，殷然將鼓，一則曰必為偃月，一則曰必為魚麗，三軍萬夫，環旋翔羊晃駭之間，虜騎乘之，遂取吾之鼓旗，此不專任責成之過，其敗五也。

translations.literal: The supreme commander cannot command alone—favored courtiers and edict envoys come in rotation to direct him; battle lines are forming, drums about to sound, when one cries 'Must be Crescent formation!' and another 'Must be Fish-scale formation!'—a hundred thousand in the three armies, wheeling like scattered sheep in alarm, and barbarian cavalry seize the moment and take our banners and drums—this is the fault of divided command and abdicated responsibility; the fifth defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander cannot command alone—favored courtiers and edict envoys come in rotation to direct him. Battle lines are forming, drums about to sound, when one cries 'Crescent formation!' and another 'Fish-scale formation!'—a hundred thousand men wheeling like scattered sheep, and enemy cavalry seize our banners. The fifth defeat: divided command and abdicated responsibility.

sentences.zh: 今者誠欲調持干戈，灑掃垢污，以為萬世安，而乃踵前非，是不可為也。」

translations.literal: Now if one truly wishes to tune and hold arms, sweep away filth, and make peace for ten thousand generations—yet tread in former errors—this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: If we truly mean to take up arms, sweep away corruption, and secure peace for ten thousand generations—yet follow old errors—it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 又作《守論》，以為：「今之議者皆曰：夫倔強之徒，吾以良將勁兵為銜策，高位美爵充飽其腸，安而不撓，外而不拘，亦猶豢擾虎狼而不指其心，則忿氣不萌。

translations.literal: He also wrote "On Defense," holding: "Today's debaters all say: toward the stubborn strongmen, use fine generals and crack troops as bit and reins, fill their bellies with high rank and noble titles, leave them at ease and unprovoked, keep them outside and unrestrained—like taming tigers and wolves without touching their hearts, so that wrath never stirs.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote On Defense, arguing: "Today's debaters all say: toward the stubborn strongmen, use fine generals and crack troops as bit and reins, fill their bellies with high rank and noble titles, leave them at ease and unprovoked, keep them outside and unrestrained—like taming tigers and wolves without touching their hearts, so that wrath never stirs.

sentences.zh: 此大歷、貞元所以守邦也，亦何必疾戰，焚煎吾民，然後以為快也！

translations.literal: This is how the Dali and Zhenyuan eras defended the realm—why must we rush to battle and burn and torment our people before we feel satisfied!
translations.idiomatic: This is how the Dali and Zhenyuan eras 'defended the realm'—why must we rush to battle and burn our own people before we feel satisfied!

sentences.zh: 愚曰：大歷、貞元之間，適以此為禍也。

translations.literal: The fool says: in the Dali and Zhenyuan periods, it was precisely this that became the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: I say: in the Dali and Zhenyuan periods, this very policy was the disaster.

sentences.zh: 當是之時，有城數十，千百卒夫，則朝廷別待之，貸以法度。

translations.literal: At that time, one with several dozen cities and a thousand or so soldiers received special treatment from the court—leniency in law.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man with a few dozen towns and a thousand or so soldiers received special treatment from court—leniency in law.

sentences.zh: 於是乎闊視大言，自樹一家，破制削法，角為尊奢，天子養威而不問，有司守恬而不呵。

translations.literal: Thereupon they stared boldly and spoke grandly, set themselves up as a house apart, broke regulations and pared laws, vied in arrogance and luxury—the Son of Heaven preserved their prestige and did not inquire; officials kept quiet and did not rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Then they stared boldly and spoke grandly, set themselves up as a house apart, broke regulations and pared laws, vied in arrogance and luxury—the Son of Heaven preserved their prestige and did not inquire; officials kept quiet and did not rebuke.

sentences.zh: 王侯通爵，越祿受之；

translations.literal: They exchanged princely titles and received rank beyond their salary;
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged princely titles and received rank beyond their salary;

sentences.zh: 覲聘不來，幾杖扶之；

translations.literal: when they skipped court audiences, canes were sent to support them;
translations.idiomatic: when they skipped court audiences, the throne sent canes to support them;

sentences.zh: 逆息虜胤，皇子嬪之；

translations.literal: when rebellious barbarian offspring needed brides, imperial princes married them;
translations.idiomatic: when rebellious barbarian offspring needed brides, imperial princes married them;

sentences.zh: 裝緣采飾，無不備之。

translations.literal: trappings, finery, and ornaments—nothing was not provided.
translations.idiomatic: trappings, finery, and ornaments—nothing was withheld.

sentences.zh: 是以地益廣，兵益強，僭擬益甚，侈心益昌。

translations.literal: Therefore territory grew broader, armies stronger, presumption deeper, extravagant hearts more flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus their territory widened, their armies strengthened, their presumption deepened, their extravagance flourished.

sentences.zh: 於是土田名器，分劃殆盡，而賊夫貪心，未及畔岸，遂有淫名越號，或帝或王，盟詛自立，恬淡不畏，走兵四略以飽其志者也。

translations.literal: Thereupon land, titles, and insignia were nearly all carved up; yet before these thieves' greedy hearts reached the brink of rebellion, some took unlawful names and exalted titles, calling themselves emperors or kings, swearing oaths and proclaiming independence, serene and fearless, sending armies in four directions to sate their ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon land, titles, and insignia were nearly all carved up; before these thieves had even reached the brink of open revolt, some took unlawful names and exalted titles, calling themselves emperors or kings, swearing oaths and proclaiming independence, serene and fearless, sending armies in four directions to sate their ambitions.

sentences.zh: 是以趙、魏、燕、齊卓起大唱，梁、蔡、吳、蜀躡而和之；

translations.literal: Therefore Zhao, Wei, Yan, and Qi rose in chorus; Liang, Cai, Wu, and Shu followed in harmony;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, Wei, Yan, and Qi rose in chorus; Liang, Cai, Wu, and Shu followed in harmony;

sentences.zh: 其餘混澒項軒囂，欲相效者，往往而是。

translations.literal: the rest, in tumult straining at their yokes and clamoring, wishing to imitate them, were everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: and countless others in the tumult, straining at their yokes, eager to imitate them, were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 運遭孝武，宵旰不忘，前英後傑，夕思朝議，故能大者誅鋤，小者惠來。

translations.literal: Fortune brought Emperor Xiaowu, who ate late and rose early without rest; former worthies and later heroes debated evening and morning—therefore the great were executed and cut down, the small won over with grace.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune brought Emperor Xiaowu, who ate late and rose early without rest; former worthies and later heroes debated morning and evening—so the great were executed, the small won over with grace.

sentences.zh: 不然，周、秦之郊，幾為獵哉！

translations.literal: Otherwise the suburbs of Zhou and Qin would nearly have become hunting grounds!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the suburbs of Zhou and Qin would nearly have become hunting grounds!

sentences.zh: 大抵生人油然多欲，欲而不得則怒，怒則爭亂隨之，是以教笞於家，刑罰於國，征伐於天下，此所以裁其欲而塞其爭也。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, the living are naturally full of desire; denied, they grow angry; anger brings strife and chaos—hence instruction and the rod in the family, punishment in the state, campaigns under heaven—this is how desire is trimmed and contention blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Human beings are naturally full of desire; denied, they grow angry; anger breeds strife and chaos. Hence instruction and the rod in the family, punishment in the state, campaigns under heaven—means to trim desire and block contention.

sentences.zh: 大歷、貞元之間，盡反此道，提區區之有而塞無涯之爭，是以首尾指支，幾不能相運掉也。

translations.literal: In the Dali and Zhenyuan eras this was wholly reversed—holding a tiny stake against boundless contention—therefore head, tail, fingers, and limbs could scarcely move together.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali and Zhenyuan eras this was wholly reversed—holding a tiny stake against boundless contention until head, tail, fingers, and limbs could scarcely move together.

sentences.zh: 今者不知非此，而反用以為經。

translations.literal: Today men do not recognize this error—they take it instead as permanent doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Today men do not recognize this error—they take it instead as permanent doctrine.

sentences.zh: 愚見為盜者非止於河北而已，嗚呼！

translations.literal: In the fool's view the robbers are not limited to Hebei alone—alas!
translations.idiomatic: In my view the robbers are not limited to Hebei alone. Alas!

sentences.zh: 大歷、貞元守邦之術，永戒之哉！」

translations.literal: The Dali and Zhenyuan method of defending the realm—let it be forever warned against!"
translations.idiomatic: Let the Dali and Zhenyuan method of 'defending the realm' be forever warned against!"

sentences.zh: 又注《孫子》，為之序，以為：「兵者，刑也；

translations.literal: He also annotated the Art of War and wrote a preface, holding: "War is punishment;
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated the Art of War and wrote a preface, holding: "War is punishment;

sentences.zh: 刑者，政事也；

translations.literal: punishment is governance;
translations.idiomatic: punishment is governance;

sentences.zh: 為夫子之徒，實仲由、冉有之事也。

translations.literal: for disciples of the Master, it was truly the business of Zhong You and Ran You.
translations.idiomatic: for disciples of the Master, it was truly the business of Zhong You and Ran You.

sentences.zh: 不知自何代何人分為二道曰文、武，離而俱行，因使縉紳之士不敢言兵，或恥言之；

translations.literal: Who knows from which age or by what hand the Two Ways of civil and military were split apart and pursued separately—so that gentry scholars dared not speak of war, or shame to speak of it;
translations.idiomatic: Who knows from which age or by what hand the Two Ways of civil and military were split apart and pursued separately—so that gentry scholars dared not speak of war, or shame to speak of it;

sentences.zh: 苟有言者，世以為粗暴異人，人不比數。

translations.literal: if any did speak, the age considered him crude and strange, someone not to be counted among their kind.
translations.idiomatic: if any did speak, the age considered him crude and strange, someone not to be counted among their kind.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 亡失根本，斯最為甚！

translations.literal: To lose the root—nothing is more grave!
translations.idiomatic: To lose the root—nothing is more grave!

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：『四郊多壘，此卿大夫之辱也。』

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: 'When ramparts multiply around the four suburbs, this is the disgrace of ministers and grandees.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says: 'When ramparts multiply around the four suburbs, this is the disgrace of ministers and grandees.'

sentences.zh: 歷觀自古，樹立其國，滅亡其國，未始不由兵也。

translations.literal: Surveying antiquity, founding a state or destroying one—never did it happen without armies.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying antiquity, founding a state or destroying one—never did it happen without armies.

sentences.zh: 主兵者必聖賢、材能、多聞博識之士乃能有功，議於廊廟之上，兵形已成，然後付之於將。

translations.literal: Only sage, talented, learned, and broad-minded men can master war with success—debating in the hall of state until the shape of the campaign is set, then entrusting execution to generals.
translations.idiomatic: Only sage, talented, learned, and broad-minded men can master war with success—debating in the hall of state until the shape of the campaign is set, then entrusting execution to generals.

sentences.zh: 漢祖言『指蹤者人也，獲兔者犬也』，此其是也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han said, 'The pointer is a man; the hound that catches the rabbit is a dog'—just so.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han said, 'The pointer is a man; the hound that catches the rabbit is a dog'—just so.

sentences.zh: 彼為相者曰：「兵非吾事，吾不當知。」

translations.literal: Yet there are chancellors who say: "War is not my affair—I need not know of it."
translations.idiomatic: Yet there are chancellors who say, "War is not my affair—I need not know of it."

sentences.zh: 君子曰：「勿居其位可也！」」

translations.literal: The gentleman says: "Then do not hold the post!""
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman says, "Then do not hold the post!""

sentences.zh: 前邠寧行軍司馬鄭注，依倚王守澄，權勢熏灼，上深惡之。

translations.literal: The former Chief of Staff of Binning, Zheng Zhu, leaned on Wang Shoucheng; his power blazed; the Emperor hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The former chief of staff of Binning, Zheng Zhu, leaned on Wang Shoucheng; his power blazed; the Emperor hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙寅，侍御史李款閣內奏彈註：「內通敕使，外連朝士，兩地往來，卜射財賄，晝伏夜動，干竊化權，人不敢言，道路以目。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingyin, Censor Li Kuan memorialized in the palace denouncing Zhu: "He communicates within with edict envoys and without with court officials; traveling between both realms, he gambles and scatters bribes; active by night and hidden by day, he steals transforming power; men dare not speak—eyes alone mark the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingyin, Censor Li Kuan memorialized in the palace denouncing Zheng Zhu: "He communicates within with edict envoys and without with court officials; traveling between both realms, he gambles and scatters bribes; active by night and hidden by day, he steals transforming power; men dare not speak—eyes alone mark the road.

sentences.zh: 請付法司。」

translations.literal: I ask that he be handed to the judicial authorities."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be handed to the judicial authorities."

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，章數十上。

translations.literal: Within ten days dozens of memorials were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days dozens of memorials were submitted.

sentences.zh: 守澄匿注於右軍，左軍中尉韋元素、樞密使楊承和、王踐言皆惡注。

translations.literal: Shoucheng hid Zhu in the Right Army. Left Army Director Wei Yuansu and Chief Palace Commissioners Yang Chenghe and Wang Jianyan all hated Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng hid Zhu in the Right Army. Left Army Director Wei Yuansu and Chief Palace Commissioners Yang Chenghe and Wang Jianyan all hated Zhu.

sentences.zh: 左軍將李弘楚說元素曰：鄭注奸猾無雙，卵鷇不除，使成羽翼，必為國患。

translations.literal: Left Army general Li Hongchu said to Yuansu: Zheng Zhu's cunning is unmatched. If the egg is not crushed before the fledgling grows wings, he will surely become a national disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Left Army general Li Hongchu said to Yuansu: Zheng Zhu's cunning is unmatched. If the egg is not crushed before the fledgling grows wings, he will surely become a national disaster.

sentences.zh: 今因御史所劾匿軍中，弘楚請以中尉意，詐為有疾，召使治之，來則中尉延與坐，弘楚侍側，伺中尉舉目，擒出杖殺之。

translations.literal: Now that he hides in the army because of the censor's charges, Hongchu asks: feign illness on the Director's behalf, summon Zhu to treat it; when he comes, the Director receives him and sits with him while Hongchu waits at his side; at the Director's glance, seize Zhu, drag him out, and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he hides in the army because of the censor's charges, Hongchu asks: feign illness on the Director's behalf, summon Zhu to treat it; when he comes, the Director receives him and sits with him while Hongchu waits at his side; at the Director's glance, seize Zhu, drag him out, and beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 中尉因見上叩頭請罪，具言其奸，楊、王必助中尉進言。

translations.literal: The Director then sees the Emperor, kowtows to confess, recounts Zhu's crimes in full—Yang and Wang will surely help the Director speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Director then sees the Emperor, kowtows to confess, recounts Zhu's crimes in full—Yang and Wang will surely help the Director speak.

sentences.zh: 況中尉有翼戴之功，豈以除奸而獲罪乎！
